title: Small-Church Elders, Here’s How to Give Your Pastor a Sabbatical
summary: Our church has 74 members and two lay elders. Here’s how we raised up five men to preach seven expository sermons and give our pastor a summer sabbatical.
summary_zh: 我们的教会共有74名会友和两名平信徒长老。以下是我们如何培养五位弟兄来宣讲七篇解经性讲道，并让我们的牧师度过一个夏季安息假。
title_zh: 小型教会的长老们，以下是为你们的牧师安排安息假的方式
content: “He should have had a sabbatical six years ago,” my fellow elder said. “I know,” I said. “We know he needs it, but how are we going to do this? We have full-time jobs and young families.” “Well, the cattle on thousand hills are the Lord’s. Let’s ask him to provide it.” I nodded in agreement, but honestly, cattle felt like less of an ask for our church. Our church consists of 74 members. We have one full-time pastor and two lay elders. And yet, exactly two years after that initial elders’ meeting, we managed to give our pastor a much-needed, six-week summer sabbatical. Five male members of our church delivered seven expository and Christ-exalting sermons. God was glorified, our pastor rested, and our church loved it. We preached through an entire book of the Bible (Habakkuk). We preached a doctrinal sermon from our confession of faith (on baptism and Communion). Two men preached for the first time. The men ranged from age 20 to 46, and I was the seasoned preacher with 25 sermons under my belt. So how did we pull this off? 1. We prayed. We knew we couldn’t do this. Only God could. This reality framed our prayers over the next two years. God was glorified, our pastor rested, and our church loved it. We came to realize that just as the Sabbath was a gift from God to man (Mark 2:27), so a sabbatical is a gift from God to a pastor. As lay elders, we were called to take steps of faith to this end while relying on the Holy Spirit’s leading and enablement. Just as Jesus is Lord of the Sabbath (Matt. 12:8), so too is he Lord of a sabbatical. As we began to make plans, we prayed that we’d hold them with an open hand and continually lay them at the feet of Jesus. We borrowed words from Jehoshaphat (2 Chron. 20:12) for our prayer in this season: “Lord, we do not know what to do, but our eyes are on you.” 2. We planned backward. We began by identifying the ideal time of year for the sabbatical. We landed on July and August, since that’s when church programming is minimal and vacations are in vogue among our congregation. This decision indirectly led us to the length of sabbatical we felt could responsibly plan for: six weeks. From there, we planned backward. The first Sunday we discussed was the Sunday our pastor would return. How did we want our brother and his wife to reintegrate into the church? We decided we wanted him to feel the warmth of our church’s love in his homecoming without being distracted by sermon preparation. So we chose to begin and end his sabbatical on Fridays. This meant our pastor had a workweek before leaving, so he could help with administrative functions. And by returning from the sabbatical on a Friday, he’d be able to join us for an elder meeting to get updates on members prior to attending church two days later. Preaching could wait another week. We created a two-year timeline that included all of the specific events and developments we thought could be feasible with the Lord’s help. This timeline helped us to answer several looming questions: Should we start the sabbatical by sending our pastor somewhere to create physical and emotional separation between him and our congregation? We agreed we should. We also felt this was an opportunity to invite our church to be generous and to tangibly show their love to our pastor of 12 years and his wife by paying for this trip. How many of our male members would be willing to assist with the preaching? We estimated three to four. How and when would we get them trained? This was the hardest question to answer but also the most rewarding part of this process. 3. We created a brotherhood. We realized our biggest hurdle would be recruiting and training men to aid in the preaching. To address the issue, we settled on offering a six-week preaching cohort during the summer prior to the sabbatical. title: Where Our Criminal Justice System Breaks Down (with Matt Martens)
summary: Matt Martens joins Collin Hansen to discuss justice, citizenship, and Christian responsibility.
summary_zh: 马特·马滕斯（Matt Martens）与柯林·汉森（Collin Hansen）一同探讨正义、公民身份和基督徒的责任。
title_zh: 我们的刑事司法制度在哪些方面存在缺陷（与Matt Martens合著）
content: When you really want to dive into the details of big questions about public policy—how we can live better together—you run into two problems: The experts and other stakeholders don’t want to consider Christian arguments, and Christians don’t want to engage in the details. That combination of a Christian argument from a legal expert was rare when Matt Martens’s book Reforming Criminal Justice: A Christian Proposal came out in 2023 from Crossway. And it’s still rare today. Matt is a trial lawyer and partner at an international law firm in Washington, DC. He and his wife are members at Capitol Hill Baptist Church, and they have two sons and a daughter. I read this book when it came out, and it’s stuck with me. Just the other day, I was thinking about the book when talking to one of my pastors, who was preparing to preach from 1 Peter on justice and obeying authorities. I thought about how I’d want to see the criminal justice system reformed if there were a good shot I’d be either a victim or criminal defendant. Isn’t that the law summed up in loving our neighbors as ourselves? From the death penalty to AI to the decline of violent crime—Matt and I covered a great deal. In This Episode 00:00 – Why poor defendants often lack adequate legal representation 02:00 – The biggest misconception about the American criminal justice system 03:32 – The criminal justice reform Matt would prioritize first 07:21 – DNA evidence, wrongful convictions, and the fallibility of the system 13:26 – Why Matt opposes the death penalty as currently practiced 19:43 – Why preaching the gospel doesn’t eliminate our responsibility to pursue public justice 22:23 – Why Christians should serve on juries 27:38 – What decades as a lawyer taught Matt about how justice actually works 39:56 – Raymond Flanks: faith after nearly 39 years of wrongful imprisonment 46:26 – How AI could transform legal work and expand access to justice Resources Mentioned: Reforming Criminal Justice by Matthew T. title: The Cumulative Effect of Thousands of Family Bible Times
summary: When your kids are inattentive or disruptive, don’t be overly discouraged. If the milk spills, if a fight erupts, all is not lost.
summary_zh: 当您的孩子注意力不集中或行为扰乱时，不要过于沮丧。如果牛奶洒了，如果发生了争吵，一切都还没完。
title_zh: 数千次家庭查经的累积效应
content: The alarm goes off, and another busy day begins. Getting kids up and ready for school, meal prep, work, after-school activities. Before you know it, the day is racing to its close. And you’re exhausted again. As Christian parents, we want our lives to count for Christ. We sincerely want our children to live their lives for Christ too. We want them to be changed by the same amazing grace that has transformed us. But how does this happen? How can we find the time and energy to effectively disciple our kids? Where will we find the creativity and passion to teach them what matters most? If you’re discouraged by your limited time and ability to shepherd your children, consider the cumulative effects of thousands of family Bible readings over the course of many years. Think Small What if a brief Bible reading today, a couple more later this week, and a few more next week eventually became a pattern, a deeply rooted habit for your family? Small investments of time and intentionality can make a big difference over a couple decades. Small investments of time and intentionality can make a big difference over the span of a couple decades. Years ago, Trevin Wax wrote an article titled “ 1000 Sermons Will Change Your Life .” What he says to pastors about preaching also applies to parents who lead their kids in family Bible reading: Pastors, don’t underestimate the cumulative effect of your preaching. You are not dumping information into brains. You are forming the habits of your people, teaching them how to read and understand and apply the Bible for themselves. Similarly in family life, our discipleship has cumulative effects that may not come to fruition for years. As parents, we’re in this for the long haul. If your children live in your home from birth to age 18, that’s 6,570 days. If you read the Bible together on average every third day, that’s 2,190 Bible readings over the course of your sons’ and daughters’ childhood and teenage years. Keep that big picture in mind when you feel defeated after a couple days on the go, when those family discipleship moments have eluded you. Think of Timothy, who was acquainted with the sacred writings from childhood because of his mother’s and grandmother’s faithful witness (2 Tim. 1:5; 3:14–15). May we be influential parents like them, who little by little and day by day pass on our life of faith to the next generation. Be Consistent, Establish a Habit With the long view in mind, think small in terms of your goals for this week, month, or year. Aim for consistency, for establishing a habit that you can pray will take root in your kids’ lives. Joe Carter recently shared the results of a sociological study of how faith moves across generations. He summarized the findings: The behaviors that most strongly predict lasting faith are active and verbal: praying together as a family, saying grace, embedding faith in the rhythm of the week rather than reserving it for Sunday, and, above all, talking about it. Children raised in homes where faith was discussed at least several times a week were more than twice as likely to attend church, pray daily, and rate religion as very important in young adulthood. The simplest way to put this truth into practice in your home is by creating a rhythm of opening the Bible regularly, reading some verses, and discussing them. You may never have a sense that one particular devotional was transformative. But keep at it. When your kids are inattentive or disruptive, don’t be overly discouraged. If the milk spills, if a fight erupts, all is not lost. Resist the temptation to quit. Come back to the reading the next day, or the day after that. Keep finding times to open the Bible with your family. Let the Word Do the Heavy Lifting Another deterrent that may get in the way of family discipleship is “the intimidation factor.” If you feel ill-equipped to teach the Bible to your kids, you may be inclined to leave that task to Sunday school teachers and youth pastors. title: Young Adults Are Hungry. Here Are 3 Ways to Feed Them.
summary: Gen Z’s hunger for food, people, and the Word gives the church a magnificent opportunity in this moment.
summary_zh: Gen Z对食物的渴望, 人们,
title_zh: 年轻的成年人是饿了。 这里有3种喂食方法。
content: When we opened the century-old church doors on the corner of Whaley Street and Wayne Street, we figured we’d have about 50 folks step through them that night. It was a Bible class for Gen Z, after all. How many Gen Zers actually want to learn about the Bible? Apparently, more than 50. We had to scramble for more chairs. It quickly became obvious that this generation—my generation—is hungry for the Bible, and we’ll starve if we don’t get fed. How are you feeding the hungry young adults in your context? My church has learned key lessons about feeding college students and young adults. These aren’t novel, but I hope they can help your people as much as they’ve helped ours. 1. Food (Like, Actual Food) I was sitting across from a leader at a major university recently and asked him how we could influence the students on that campus. He looked at me and said the plainest thing: “Food wins.” To win the heart of a man, you go through the stomach. If you want to feed people the gospel, consider first feeding them a sandwich. This is why my brother (“Chef Chunk” as they call him) has been serving an incredible amount of pancake batter out of a four-foot plastic storage container, complete with chocolate chips, blueberries, and a few other cheap toppings. We start pancake-flipping before 7 p.m. and don’t stop until we start class at 8:03 p.m., to keep up with the demand. Apparently breakfast for dinner is a fan favorite. Eating meals with others is one of the greatest indicators of personal well-being—the more we eat with our families (whether spiritual or biological), the more likely we are to be satisfied with our lives and filled with love, joy, and peace. Yet we’re eating fewer meals together than ever. What if the church was one of the great combatants of this damaging trend? 2. Friends (Like, Actual Friends) Speaking of loneliness, our culture is increasingly lacking “third spaces” where lonely people can find and build community. Robert Putnam described and predicted this decades ago in Bowling Alone —but these days we don’t just bowl alone. We shop alone, eat alone, entertain alone. We even tend to date or do friendship “alone,” as in virtually rather than in person. What few third spaces remain—the gym, sports environments, coffee shops—aren’t ideal for making meaningful connections. In gyms, we have our headphones on; at sports games, the music is so loud you get hoarse when you speak; and coffee shops are great but usually filled with headphones-on, screened-off people (and $7 lattes). Fresh-out-of-college Jimmy has nowhere to meet potential-best-friend Johnny or potential-love-of-his-life Jessica. That leaves Jimmy feeling hopeless in one of the most foundational needs of life: relationships. Our culture is increasingly lacking ‘third spaces’ where lonely people can find and build community. Yet this is a hole best filled by the new humanity God created called the church. Amid a growing cultural hunger for embodied friendships, maybe one of the major ways our church can “seek the welfare” of our cities (Jer. 29:7) is to build environments where a wide variety of folks can congregate. Maybe that looks like creating spaces for line-dancing, pick-up basketball, or weekly pickleball nights. But I have a hunch that one of the most interesting third spaces we can create might not need to be about entertainment. 3. Knowledge (Like, Spiritual Knowledge) “Do you know what Christmas is about?” “Um—not sure. What do you mean?” “Like, do you know the story behind it?” “Hmm. I feel like it’s about a guy . . .” “YES! Do you know his name?” “Mmm. Nah man.” “Jesus. His name is Jesus.” This is a real conversation I had with an average high school student in the South, the heart of the so-called Bible Belt. I could tell you of dozens of other conversations just like it. Here’s the truth: The Bible is the most interesting story in the world, and no one knows it anymore. 如果教会是这种破坏性趋势的伟大战士之一呢? 2. 朋友(如实际朋友) 说到孤独,我们的文化越来越缺乏“第三空间”,人们可以在那里找到和建设社区。 罗伯特·普特南(Robert Putnam)在几十年前, 我们单独购物 单独吃饭 单独娱乐

title: The Festive Attire We Really Need
summary: Even in our finest clothes we can still be dirty on the inside. Advent reminds us that Jesus dresses us in his righteousness.
summary_zh: 即使穿着我们最好的衣服 内心还是可以脏的 基督提醒我们,耶稣穿戴我们的正义。
title_zh: 我们真正需要的节奏
content: Read He will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver, and he will purify the sons of Levi and refine them like gold and silver, and they will bring offerings in righteousness to the LORD. Then the offering of Judah and Jerusalem will be pleasing to the LORD as in the days of old and as in former years. (Mal. 3:3–4) Reflect My grandmother always made going to church a special event. She helped me pick the right dress, made sure my shoes were shiny and clean, and withstood burns from the curling iron to perfect my hairdo. I know church attire can vary. But I still get dressed up for corporate worship because, no matter how cliché it sounds, I want to wear my Sunday best for Jesus. Yet even in our finest clothes, we can still be dirty on the inside. Hidden sins are, after all, hidden. We can sing hymns at max volume, forgetting the way we treated our coworkers last week. We can kneel in prayer, easily dismissing what we posted on the internet earlier that morning. We can take the bread and wine even if we lost it with our kids in the car. People at church only see what’s on the outside, but God looks on the heart (1 Sam. 16:7). And unless we come clean, we can’t come into his presence at all. Even in our finest clothes, we can still be dirty on the inside. Purity in God’s presence is a major theme in Scripture. In Leviticus, we learn how Israel was to distinguish between the clean and unclean. These categories extended to foods and animals. Even people could be defiled by disease or by touching unclean things such as a dead body. The temple was off-limits for the unclean. Only ritual washings and animal sacrifices made reentry into God’s presence achievable. But even this wasn’t permanent—for the blood of bulls and goats couldn’t fully atone for sin (Heb. 10:4). Like Israel, we dare not present ourselves before God in our sinful condition. As the psalmist asks, “Who shall stand in [God’s] holy place? He who has clean hands and a pure heart” (Ps. 24:3–4). While soap and water might wash our filthy hands, what can purify our sin-stained hearts? In today’s verses, the prophet Malachi announced the coming of One who would refine his people as gold and silver. Later, the author of Hebrews clarified the refiner’s identity: If the blood of goats and bulls . . . sanctify for the purification of the flesh, how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, purify our conscience from dead works to serve the living God. (Heb. 9:13–14) During Advent, we remember that Jesus is the great Refiner. He came to shed his purifying blood to cover our sins and forgive us. Then, like a refiner who heats metal to remove impurities, the Lord sanctifies us so that on judgment day we’ll be an unblemished offering to God. On that day, because of Jesus, we’ll wear white robes of righteousness (Rev. 6:11). Grandma made sure I looked pretty for church, but I wasn’t truly clean. Jesus, the great Purifier of sinners, is the only One who can wash away every stain and remove every impurity. When he dresses us in white robes, we’ll enter God’s presence because we’ll be clean—not just on the outside but on the inside too. Respond Sometimes the Lord refines us through trials and difficult circumstances. How have you experienced his refining process this year? Write a prayer thanking God for Christ who cleanses, purifies, and refines us so we’ll one day be holy and acceptable in his presence.
content_zh:
读取 他必坐作炼银的精炼者,他必洗涤利未之子,并如金银般精炼,他们必以善报主耶和华. 犹大和耶路撒冷的供奉,将像往年和往年一样,为耶和华所喜悦。 (3:3-4) 反映 我奶奶总是把去教堂做成一件特殊的事

她帮我选合适的裙子 确保我的鞋子光亮洁洁 从卷曲的铁里烧伤 我知道教堂的服装会有所不同 但我还是穿好衣服去参加公司礼拜 因为不管这听起来多么陈词滥调 我想穿我的星期天最好的耶稣。 即便穿着我们最好的衣服 我们内心仍然可以肮脏

隐藏的罪恶毕竟是隐藏的。 我们可以用最高音量唱颂歌 忘记上周我们对待同事的方式 我们可以跪在祷告中, 轻易地放弃我们当天早晨在互联网上发布的内容。 我们可以拿走面包和酒 即使我们失去了它与我们的孩子在车里。 人们在教堂只看到外面的东西,但上帝看着心脏(1Sam. 16:7).

除非我们坦白,否则我们根本无法进入他的存在。 即使穿着我们最好的衣服, 我们内部仍然可以脏。 上帝面前的纯洁是圣经中的一个主要主题。 在利维提库斯,我们了解到以色列如何区分干净和不干净。 这些类别扩大到食物和动物。

甚至人们也可能因疾病或触摸尸体等不干净的东西而受到玷污。 该寺对不洁者禁入. 只有仪式洗涤和动物牺牲才能使重返上帝的存在。 但即使是这也不是永久的 — — 因为公牛和山羊的血无法完全赎罪(Heb. 10:4)。

与以色列一样,我们不敢在罪恶的条件下站在上帝面前。 正如诗人所问的, " 谁会站在[上帝]的圣地? 手清净而心清净者”(第24:3-4页)。 虽然肥皂和水可能洗我们的脏手,但什么能净化我们的罪恶的心? 先知马拉奇在今天的诗文中宣布,

后来,希伯来人的作者澄清了提炼者的身份: 如果山羊和公牛的血... ...为净化肉体而神圣化, 基督的血会有多少, 他通过永恒的灵献给自己 没有污垢上帝, (Heb. 9:13-14)在"启示录"中,我们记得耶稣是伟大的炼油者.

他为了掩盖我们的罪孽 并原谅我们而来 然后,像精炼者一样,他用金属加热去除杂质,主使我们圣洁,这样,在审判日,我们将成为向上帝献礼的无瑕疵者。 因为耶稣的缘故, 外婆确保我看起来很适合教堂,

耶稣,罪人的伟大净化者,是唯一可以洗去每一个污点,去除每一个杂质的人. 当他穿白袍时, 我们将进入上帝的面前, 有时主会通过考验和困难的环境来完善我们 你今年是怎么经历他的提炼过程的?

感谢上帝净化、净化、精炼我们,

title: Don’t Be Afraid of the Alien Question
summary: ‘Faith in Space’ shows that many Americans throughout history have already taken the question of extraterrestrial life seriously, but they’ve done so from outside an orthodox Christian framework.
summary_zh: ”“宇宙信仰”表明, 历史上许多美国人已经认真对待地球外生命问题,
title_zh: 不要害怕外星人的问题
content: Have you ever wondered whether other worlds exist, and, if they do, whether they’re filled with intelligent life? If so, you’ve tapped into a deeply human instinct. Americans have long looked up at the night sky and asked that question. For Christians, though, the answers can feel unnerving. We already believe in nonhuman intelligence. We call them angels and demons. But aliens would be something else—material, embodied, literally otherworldly . In 2016, NASA started a conversation among religious scholars at the Center of Theological Inquiry in Princeton about what the existence of extraterrestrial life would mean for religion. Paul Gutjahr, Ruth N. Halls professor of English at Indiana University, has been wrestling with that question for years. Faith in Space: American Religious Belief in Extraterrestrial Life is his considered answer. He thinks we need to look back at existing “extraterrestrial cosmologies” in American religions rather than merely pondering future possibilities (7). Faith in Space is ultimately a history of what happens when religious communities take extraterrestrial life seriously. Many minority religions have, and it has shaped their cosmology and even their soteriology. But for many evangelical Christians, Gutjahr’s history raises a more uncomfortable question: What happens when we don’t take seriously the possibility of extraterrestrial life? Alien Religion Early Americans didn’t need much help imagining inhabited worlds. According to Gutjahr, many Americans “believed there to be life elsewhere in the universe” (19). By the end of the 19th century, “every stratum of American society had been exposed” to this belief (43). For example, Emanuel Swedenborg taught that the universe is populated with humans bearing God’s image and claimed to have conversed with them. His American followers never numbered more than a few thousand, and yet his ideas traveled across the young nation; Helen Keller held them, as did John Chapman (a.k.a. Johnny Appleseed). What happens when we don’t take seriously the possibility of extraterrestrial life? Andrew Jackson Davis, the father of American Spiritualism, was similarly inspired, convinced that “if life is to be found on other planets, it is human life.” He arranged extraterrestrial humans in “a progression of degrees that move from less to more spiritual” (64). Then Joseph Smith took things further. Latter-day Saints (Mormons) took an “aggressive extraterrestrial cosmological stance,” linking all worlds under one governing structure (79). God created many inhabited worlds arranged in “a hierarchy where some worlds rule over others” (89). Among these many worlds, Earth holds the least desirable title of “the most wicked, and thus most in need of a savior” (86). God himself is an enfleshed exalted man dwelling on a planet near the star Kolob. I’d add that the Salt Lake Temple bears the Big Dipper, and early Latter-day Saint temple iconography is thick with suns, moons, and stars. Next came the founder of Seventh-day Adventism, Ellen G. White. Where William Miller’s followers read comets and meteor showers as signs of Christ’s return, White gave Seventh-day Adventists “a far more complex understanding of their relationship with the stars” (124). Ours “was the only wicked world” (125). White distinguished strongly between the righteous and unrighteous worlds, and put Earth on the wrong side of that distinction. By the 20th century, the heavens were packed and theories about the heavens were part of salvation. Then comes Helena Blavatsky (Theosophy), L. Ron Hubbard (Scientology), Wallace Fard Muhammad and Louis Farrakhan (Nation of Islam), Malachi Z. York (Nuwaubian Nation), Ashtar Command, and Heaven’s Gate. All these figures or groups saw extraterrestrial life as part of the human story, whether for our good or our ill, or both. While the subtitle promises to cover American religions broadly, Gutjahr sets aside Catholics, Jews, and native traditions. The only “Protestants” h

你有没有想过其他世界是否存在,如果存在,他们是否充满了智慧生命? 如果是这样的话,你已经深入到了人类的本能之中。 美国人早就仰望着夜空,问了这个问题. 但对于基督徒来说 答案会让人不安 我们已经相信非人类智慧 我们称他们为天使和恶魔。

他的美国追随者人数从未超过几千人,然而他的想法却横跨了年轻的国家;海伦·凯勒也抱着他们,约翰·查普曼(英语:Johnny Appleseed)也是如此. 如果我们不认真对待外星生命的可能性,

美国精神主义之父安德鲁·杰克逊·戴维斯(Andrew Jackson Davis)同样受到启发,他坚信“如果在其他星球上找到生命,那就是人的生命。” 他将外星人类安排在“从较少的学位发展到更精神的学位”(64)。 后来约瑟夫·史密斯把事情更进一步.

末日圣徒(摩门教徒)采取了一种“侵略性的地外宇宙学立场,将所有的世界在一个管理结构下联系起来(79)。 上帝创造了许多有人居住的世界,这些世界是以“一些世界统治其他世界的等级”安排的(89)。 在许多世界中,地球拥有最不可取的“最邪恶因而最需要救世主”的称号(86)。

上帝本身就是一个被包围的尊贵的人, 住在一个靠近恒星科洛布的星球上。 盐湖寺内有大迪珀, 接下来是基督复临安息日会的创始人爱伦·G·怀特.

威廉·米勒的追随者将彗星和流星雨读作基督回归的标志,怀特给了基督复临安息日会信徒"对其与恒星关系的更复杂的理解"(124). 我们的“是唯一邪恶的世界”(125年)。 怀特强烈区分了正直和不公的世界,将地球置于这种区分的错误一边.

到了20世纪,诸天被收拾,关于诸天的理论是救赎的一部分. 接下来是Helena Blavatsky(Theosophy)、L. Ron Hubbard(科学学)、Wallace Fard Muhammad和Louis Farrakhan(伊斯兰联盟)、Malachi Z. York(努瓦乌比亚民族)、Ashtar指挥部和天门。

title: Fulani Militants Kill 14 Christians in Plateau State, Nigeria
summary: At least 14 Christians have been killed in fresh attacks across four local government areas of Plateau state, Nigeria, days after President Bola Ahmed Tinubu appealed for forgiveness over his failure
summary_zh: 在尼日利亚博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布总统就其未能保护人民免受袭击一事呼吁原谅的几天后，在高原州的四个地方政府辖区内发生的最新袭击中，至少有14名基督徒被杀害。
title_zh: 富拉尼武装分子在尼日利亚高原州杀害14名基督徒
content: At least 14 Christians have been killed in fresh attacks across four local government areas of Plateau state, Nigeria, days after President Bola Ahmed Tinubu appealed for forgiveness over his failure to visit violence-affected communities during an earlier trip to the state and promised to rebuild destroyed communities and return internally displaced persons (IDPs) to their ancestral homes. The killings occurred between Sunday, Nov. 15, and Monday, Nov. 16, in Mangu, Riyom, Barkin Ladi and Bokkos local government areas, according to community sources and local security groups. Armed attackers reportedly targeted rural settlements and ambushed residents traveling between communities. The latest violence followed Tinubu’s visit to Jos on Saturday, Nov. 14, for an All Progressives Congress (APC) political rally at Zaria Road Stadium, where he acknowledged the suffering of communities affected by recurring attacks and displacement. Addressing residents and party supporters, Tinubu asked Plateau residents to forgive him for not visiting affected communities during his previous trip to the state in April. “When I last visited the other time, I was limited to the airport,” he said. “Forgive me if you didn’t see me in the hinterland, but I saw the devastation. I got the report from the governor. I saw horror in the faces of our people.” The president promised to rebuild communities destroyed by violence and facilitate the return of displaced residents. “We will rebuild your communities, and we will bring you back to your communities,” Tinbu added. “I have directed all the security agencies to take decisive action and sustain peace and stability on the Plateau.” He also commended the Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Dr. Bernard Doro, for identifying vulnerable populations and coordinating humanitarian assistance. Tinubu announced that 1,000 forest guards were undergoing training and that surveillance cameras promised to Plateau state had been procured to strengthen security monitoring and early warning operations. However, fresh attacks were reported within hours of the president’s departure from the state. In Mangu Local Government Area, armed attackers invaded Zwagal community in Jipal District at about 9 p.m. on Sunday, killing nine people. Other residents were reportedly missing following the attack. Silas Nanfwang, a resident who confirmed the incident to journalists, called on security agencies to intensify efforts to locate the attackers and bring those responsible to justice. In Barkin Ladi, 79-year-old Da Ishaku Pam Vwos was killed when armed men invaded Sho village at about 5:20 p.m. on Sunday, according to the Berom Youth Moulders Association (BYM). The association’s National Publicity Secretary, Rwang Tengwong, also reported the killing of 42-year-old Dauda John Davou during an attack on the Sambak community in Hoss District, Riyom LGA, at about 2 a.m. on Sunday. Another attack was reported in the Jol community around 12:10 a.m. on Sunday. According to BYM, local vigilantes responded to the attackers, preventing further casualties. The association said the incidents followed the shooting of Joshua Doro Dafwel in Jol on Wednesday. He is currently receiving medical attention. BYM also reported that Ina Arin was killed when armed men ambushed him and his friend, Abok Gyang, as they returned to Dorong village in Foron District. Gyang survived the attack. In Bokkos Local Government Area, two people, including a unit commander of the Plateau state-owned security outfit, Operation Rainbow, were killed in an ambush on Monday afternoon. The victims, identified as Gambo and his companion, were traveling on a motorcycle from Hurti village to Tadai in Manguna District when armed men attacked them at about 1:30 p.m. They had reportedly visited Hurti for a condolence visit and died at the scene. title: Hindu Nationalists Target Christians in West Bengal, India
summary: At least 48 to 65 incidents of targeted harassment, church vandalism, and physical violence against Christian communities in West Bengal, India, have been recorded between May and November. The Bangiy
summary_zh: 据记录，5月至11月期间，印度西孟加拉邦发生了至少48至65起针对性骚扰、破坏教堂和针对基督徒社区的暴力行为。
title_zh: 印度西孟加拉邦的印度教民族主义者将矛头对准基督徒
content: At least 48 to 65 incidents of targeted harassment, church vandalism, and physical violence against Christian communities in West Bengal, India, have been recorded between May and November. The Bangiya Christiya Pariseba, a Christian organization working for the welfare of the state’s Christian community, compiled this data. The right-wing Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power in West Bengal following the April 2026 Legislative Assembly elections. Independent tracking by the research group India Hate Lab verified 60 hate crime incidents explicitly targeting Christian individuals, domestic fellowships, and institutional properties within West Bengal during the same period, confirming the widespread geographic footprint of the escalation of attacks on Christians. According to reports, the latest attack occurred on Nov. 9, when vandals desecrated a sacred shrine and Marian grotto of a church in an overnight attack in Khari Bamuner Chak, located within the Raidighi and Baruipur pastoral region of West Bengal’s South Parganas. A week earlier, a heavily organized contingent of about 40 men attacked a house prayer fellowship in Rayan village of the Bardhaman area. The assailants stormed the private residence during a morning service, violently assaulting the officiating pastor and worshippers. Surge of Attacks The surge in targeted violence, intimidation, and vandalism against Christian communities, churches, and home prayer fellowships in West Bengal is proving that Hindu nationalists have found West Bengal to be the new hunting ground with tacit support of the authorities. The state is currently experiencing a rapid breakdown in local law enforcement deterrence. This erosion directly threatens the constitutional guarantees enshrined in Article 25 of the Indian Constitution, which ensures freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion. The emergence of organized Hindutva networks operating with near-total impunity represents not merely localized social friction, but a systemic challenge to the rule of law and civil stability across the state. Faith Space Shrinking Across rural and semi-urban districts of West Bengal, Hindu nationalists increasingly employ physical blockades, structural desecration, and coordinated mob actions to shrink the space for religious minority assemblies. By weaponizing social intimidation and exploiting police inertia, these actors seek to criminalize ordinary acts of devotion, transforming private exercise of faith into contested public security triggers. Detailed documentation by human rights organizations and community defense networks attributes the vast majority of these incursions to organized Hindutva-affiliated groups. Investigations specifically point to operational coordination by local cadres associated with the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) and the Bajrang Dal, the RSS’s militant arm. Assailants consistently deploy dual narratives of illegal “unlawful religious conversions” and fabricated “honey traps.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . content_zh:
5月至11月期间,印度西孟加拉邦至少有48至65起针对基督教社区的有针对性骚扰、破坏教堂和人身暴力事件。 Bangiya Christiya Pariseba是一个致力于国家基督教团体福利的基督教组织,

右翼印度民族主义者Bharatiya Janata党(BJP)于2026年4月立法议会选举后在西孟加拉邦上台.

研究小组印度仇恨实验室的独立跟踪核实了同期60起仇恨犯罪事件,明确针对西孟加拉邦的基督教个人、家庭奖学金和机构财产,证实了对基督教徒袭击升级造成的广泛地域影响。 据报道,最近一次袭击发生在11月.

9日,在位于西孟加拉邦南帕尔干纳斯的Raigighi和Baruipur牧区Khari Bamuner Chak的一起夜间袭击中,被破坏者亵渎了一座圣地和一座教堂的Marian地道。 一周前,一支由约40名男子组成的组织严密的特遣队袭击了Bardhaman地区Rayan村的一个家庭祈祷研究金。

袭击者在上午礼拜时冲入了私人住宅,暴力袭击了牧师和礼拜者。

袭击的激增 西孟加拉邦针对基督教社区、教堂和家庭祈祷研究金的有针对性暴力、恐吓和破坏行为激增,证明印度教民族主义者在当局的默许下发现西孟加拉邦是新的狩猎地。 目前,该国地方执法威慑迅速崩溃。

这种削弱直接威胁到《印度宪法》第25条所载的宪法保障,该条确保良心自由和自由信奉、实践和传播宗教的权利。

有组织的印度人网络的出现几乎完全不受惩罚,这不仅是局部性的社会摩擦,而且是对全国法治和国内稳定的系统性挑战。

印度民族主义者在西孟加拉邦的农村和半城市地区越来越多地采取实际封锁、结构性亵渎、协调暴徒行动来缩小宗教少数群体集会的空间。

通过将社会恐吓武器化和利用警察惯性,这些行为者试图将普通的献身行为定为刑事犯罪,将个人信仰的行使转变为有争议的公共安全触发因素。 人权组织和社区防卫网络的详细文件将绝大多数入侵归因于有组织的印度教附属团体。

调查特别指向与印度印度人理事会(VHP)和RSS好战武装Bajrang Dal有关的当地干部的业务协调。 仆从们一贯使用非法的“非法宗教皈依”和捏造的“甜蜜陷阱”的双重说法。 更多新闻报导, 采访,请通过电子邮件。

title_zh: 马来西亚法院将一名皈依基督教者的宗教自由诉讼移交地区法庭
content: A 34-year-old law graduate’s multi-year battle exposes the severe reality of religious control and the legal trap facing citizens who want to leave Islam. A high-stakes constitutional challenge highlighting the erosion of religious freedom in Malaysia has taken a procedural step backward. The Kuala Lumpur High Court has ordered that a lawsuit filed by a 34-year-old legal researcher seeking legal recognition as a Christian be transferred to the Shah Alam High Court. The case lays bare the rigid and intrusive control exercised by state apparatuses and Islamic religious authorities over personal faith, showcasing a system where basic human rights — such as choosing one’s own religion — are tightly policed by the government. A Life Labeled Without Consent The plaintiff, Shameer PV, identifies as a Christian and has lived as one since he was 18. However, under strict Malaysian administrative regulations, the word “Islam” was stamped on his compulsory national identity card (MyKad) when he was just 12, following a bureaucratic policy introduced under the National Registration Act. Despite decades of personal conviction and his marriage to a Christian wife, the state continues to legally treat him as a Muslim, directly violating his parental and marital status and refusing to recognize his family. Shameer’s legal challenge names the federal government, the Selangor state government, and the Selangor Islamic Religious Council (MAIS) as defendants. He argues that labeling citizens by religion on state identity cards violates Article 11(1) of the Federal Constitution, which ostensibly guarantees every person the right to profess and practice their religion. Trapped in Shariah Bureaucracy Shameer’s ordeal underscores the labyrinthine and punishing hurdles forced upon religious minorities and converts in Malaysia’s dual-justice system, which runs a parallel set of Islamic (Shariah) courts alongside the civil judiciary. In 2018, Shameer initiated proceedings in a Selangor Shariah court seeking official recognition of his Christian faith. After an exhausting 72 court sessions spanning over seven years, the Shariah court dismissed his application in January. Rather than allowing him to move on with his life, the religious court went a step further, ordering state departments and Islamic authorities to “guide and control” his practice of Islam — effectively treating his desire to leave the faith as a disciplinary or correctional matter. Having exhausted the religious tribunal system, Shameer turned to the civil high court in July, filing an originating summons to ask the highest judicial authorities whether state-mandated religious labeling on identity cards is unconstitutional, and whether Shariah courts have any lawful jurisdiction over individuals who do not practice Islam. A Wider Crisis for Freedom of Conscience International human rights observers and religious freedom advocates have long criticized Malaysia’s legal framework regarding apostasy and conversion. While the Malaysian Constitution theoretically protects freedom of religion, civil courts have repeatedly ruled that only Islamic Shariah courts have the authority to permit someone to leave Islam — creating an effective judicial catch-22, as Shariah courts rarely grant permission to renounce the religion. For international human rights advocates and supporters of religious liberty, Shameer’s case is a stark reminder of the state-enforced religious controls facing millions in Southeast Asia. As his case moves to the Shah Alam court, the legal battle continues to test whether Malaysia’s secular constitutional framework can protect an individual’s fundamental right of conscience against a totalizing state religious bureaucracy. content_zh:
一个34岁的法学毕业生的多年战斗暴露了宗教控制的严重现实和想要离开伊斯兰教的公民所面临的法律陷阱. 马来西亚宗教自由受到侵蚀,

吉隆坡高等法院下令将34岁法律研究者提出的寻求法律承认为基督徒的诉讼移交沙阿拉姆高等法院.

这一案件暴露了国家机构和伊斯兰宗教当局对个人信仰的严格和侵扰性控制,表明政府严格控制基本人权(如选择自己的宗教)的制度。 未经同意的生活标签 原告Shameer PV确认为基督教徒,自18岁起就一直作为一个教徒生活在一起。

然而,根据严格的马来西亚行政条例,他12岁时的强制性国民身份证(MyKad)上印有“伊斯兰”一词,这是根据《国家登记法》实行的官僚政策。

尽管几十年的个人信念和他与基督教妻子的婚姻,但国家继续在法律上将他视为穆斯林,直接侵犯了他的父母和婚姻状况,并拒绝承认他的家人. 沙门的法律质疑将联邦政府,雪兰莪州政府,雪兰莪伊斯兰宗教委员会(MAIS)列为被告.

他辩称,以宗教方式将公民贴在州身份证上违反了《联邦宪法》第11(1)条,该条表面上保障每个人信奉和奉行其宗教的权利。

伊斯兰教法官僚沙姆耶的折磨凸显了Labyrinthine和惩罚强加给宗教少数派和皈依马来西亚双重司法制度的障碍,马来西亚的双重司法制度与民事司法平行设有一套伊斯兰(伊斯兰教法)法院。 2018年,沙姆耶在塞兰哥教法法院提起诉讼,寻求官方承认他的基督教信仰.

经过历时七年的72次开庭,教法法院于1月驳回了他的申请。

宗教法庭没有让他继续自己的生活,而是更进一步,命令国家部门和伊斯兰当局“指导和控制”他的伊斯兰教习俗——实际上将他放弃信仰的愿望视为纪律或惩戒事项。

在用尽了宗教法庭制度之后,Shameer于7月向民事高等法院提交了原传票,询问最高司法当局在身份证上贴上国家规定的宗教标签是否违宪,伊斯兰教法法院是否对不信奉伊斯兰教的个人拥有任何合法管辖权。

国际人权观察员和宗教自由倡导者长期批评马来西亚关于叛教和皈依的法律框架。

虽然马来西亚宪法理论上保护宗教自由,但民事法院一再裁定只有伊斯兰教法法院有权允许某人离开伊斯兰教——这创造了有效的司法抓捕-22,因为伊斯兰教法法院很少允许放弃该宗教.

对国际人权倡导者和宗教自由支持者来说,Shameer一案明确提醒人们注意东南亚数百万人所面临的国家强制宗教控制。

summary_zh: 11月1日，六人在被富拉尼族极端分子关押超过六个月后，迈出了重获自由的第一步。其中一人仅两天后就去世了。13岁的哈萨娜·布卢斯（Hasana Bulus）在被送往医院时已处于危急状态，后在医院去世。布卢斯是富拉尼民兵绑架的11人之一……   这篇题为《少女被囚禁六个月后死亡》的文章最初发表在“国际基督徒关注”网站上。
title_zh: 少女被囚禁六个月后死亡
content: On Nov. 1, six people took their first steps of freedom after being held by Fulani extremists for more than six months. One of them died only two days later. Hasana Bulus, 13, died in the hospital where she was taken in critical condition. Bulus was one of the 11 people who were kidnapped by a Fulani militia in April. One had escaped, but five died at the camp, and the rest were released with Bulus — including the 4-year-old daughter of a woman who had died in captivity. Bulus’ village, Awon, is predominantly Christian and has been the target of Fulani attacks, just like Ariko, a neighboring village in Kaduna state. According to a six-year study conducted by the Observatory for Religious Freedom in Africa (ORFA), Islamic Fulani militias are by far the deadliest persecutors of Christians in Nigeria. Ariko is home to the 37 Christians who were kidnapped during the Easter services earlier this year in a neighboring village. Of these, 17 people have died in captivity, 12 have escaped, and eight have since been released. The abductees from both these villages were held in the same forest hideout, where they were kept in inhumane conditions. “They [the villagers] told us how they would stay for two weeks without food,” one woman, whose father died in the camp, told Open Doors . “They only boil water to drink. That’s how they struggled before the bandits gave them corn flour, and they started making swallow (a porridge). The men are restrained, chained in groups; they are not free to move around.” All of the male abductees in these groups had died in the camp. Christian Solidarity Worldwide (CSW) is calling for Nigerian authorities to protect these communities and fight to free more people left in bondage. “We continue to urge the Nigerian government at state and federal levels to prioritize the protection of vulnerable communities throughout the nation, to combat the threat posed by the litany of terrorist groups that are active in the country far more effectively, and to secure the release of all abductees,” CSW CEO Scot Bower said. “Nigeria’s Christians do not need another statement of sympathy,” ICC’s president, Shawn Wright, said. “They need protection , justice , and accountability . When those who murder innocent Christians face no meaningful consequences, impunity becomes an invitation to the next attack. The Nigerian government must protect vulnerable communities, pursue the perpetrators, and make clear that these crimes will not go unanswered.” Story by Bella Agnello To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . title_zh: 刚果民主共和国曼巴萨地区在埃博拉疫情期间至少有26人死亡
content: Twenty-six people have reportedly been killed and several others abducted in a new attack carried out by the Islamist rebels of Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) on Nov. 10, during the night, in Mambasa territory, Ituri province, northeastern DR Congo, a country where nearly 93% of the population is Christian. According to a local association coordinator, Malikidogo, more than six villages were affected, including Kangwayi, Misele, Mingazi, and Mambaka. “The situation is very serious; we identified 26 people killed, several others abducted, and many families are still searching for their missing loved ones,” Malikidogo said. “Aside from the death of many people, five houses were burnt alongside some motorcycles. We are calling on the authorities to take urgent action to protect the population.” Left With Nothing Survivors who succeeded in escaping reported that many families had to run for their lives, leaving their homes and belongings behind. “We were very afraid when we realized that the enemies were already in the village when we heard people crying and others running in every direction,” one survivor said. “We just fled without having time to collect our belongings, just to save our lives. We do not know what will happen next, and we are afraid that they might come and reach Mambasa city where we are today.” The attack comes at a difficult time for local communities, which are already facing the threat of Ebola . Residents are now dealing with both the fear of the disease and the danger of further attacks. There are concerns that the violence could also make it harder to control the Ebola outbreak. People fleeing their villages may spread the disease to other communities, while insecurity could prevent health workers from reaching those who need medical help. A local leader also expressed concern about the situation and called for stronger protection of civilians. “We have suffered for many years because of the atrocities committed by ADF Islamist terrorists,” he said. “We are already struggling with Ebola, and now we are facing these attacks again. We cannot continue living like this. We are calling on the government and security forces to protect our communities before more innocent lives are lost.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . 据报告,11月10日,民主同盟军伊斯兰叛乱分子在刚果东北部伊图里省曼巴萨县发动了新的袭击,造成26人死亡,另有数人被绑架,该国近93%的人口是基督教徒。

据当地协会协调员Malikidogo说,有6个以上的村庄受到影响,其中包括Kangwayi、Misele、Mingazi和Mambaka。 “局势非常严重;我们确认有26人被杀害,另有数人被绑架,许多家庭仍在寻找失踪的亲人。”

“除了许多人的死亡外,还有五所房屋与一些摩托车一起被烧毁。 我们呼吁当局采取紧急行动保护人民。” 成功逃脱的幸存者一无所有地离开,报告说,许多家庭不得不逃命,留下家园和财物。

一位幸存者说,“当我们意识到敌人已经在村里时,我们非常害怕,当我们听到人们在哭,而其他人则朝每个方向奔跑时”。 “我们刚刚逃离,没有时间收集我们的财产,只是为了拯救我们的生命。

我们不知道接下来会发生什么,我们担心他们会来到我们今天所在的曼巴萨市。” 袭击发生在当地社区面临埃博拉威胁的困难时刻。 居民们现在正在处理对疾病的恐惧和进一步攻击的危险。

人们担心暴力也可能使控制埃博拉疫情变得更加困难。 逃离村庄的人可能把这种疾病传播到其他社区,而不安全则可能妨碍保健工作者帮助需要医疗帮助的人。 一名当地领导人还对局势表示关切,呼吁加强对平民的保护。

他说,“由于民主同盟军伊斯兰恐怖分子的暴行,我们受苦多年。” “我们已经在与埃博拉作斗争,现在我们再次面临这些袭击。 我们不能继续这样生活。 我们要求政府和安全部队在更多的无辜者丧生之前保护我们的社区。” 阅读更多新闻,

title_zh: 食堂大屠杀4天后遇害
content: Just days after the deadly massacre in Cantine, where at least 33 civilians were reportedly killed, suspected Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) fighters have struck again in Beni Territory, claiming four more lives and burning several houses in Mabalako, in the Democratic Republic of Congo. At about 12:20 a.m. on Thursday, Nov. 12, Mabalako once again faced ADF violence , with a fresh overnight attack in the Kamahume neighborhood. According to local civil society representatives, the death toll rose from an initial three to four, while more than seven houses were also set ablaze during the deadly incursion. The attack has renewed fears among civilians already traumatized by the violence that struck Cantine-Aloya less than a week earlier. The proximity of these two attacks in time and location has heightened concerns about the continuing threat posed by the ADF to civilian populations across Beni. “We are living in constant fear,” said Mulwahali, a survivor. “We have not yet recovered from the pain of what happened in Cantine, where innocent people were brutally killed and homes reduced to ashes. Now the violence has reached Mabalako, and once again we are mourning our loved ones and watching our homes burn. We do not know who will be next or where these attackers will strike again. We are even tired of burying our people without heads. All we want is to live in peace and sleep in our homes without fearing that we may never see another morning.” A Need for Security Local civil society representatives have appealed to security services to take full responsibility for protecting civilians, strengthen security operations, and prevent further attacks. Residents of Runzayi, Malondo, Ngazi, and Kibunamaru have also been urged to remain vigilant, maintain calm, and cooperate with security forces by reporting suspicious movements. “We cannot continue living at the mercy of armed attackers,” a local Catholic bishop said. “Although the intervention of the FARDC helped limit the destruction in Mabalako, the fact that the attackers could strike and disappear without their direction being known leaves us deeply frightened. We want security, not another massacre.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . After…   The post  The Girl They Killed for Refusing a Forced Marriage  first appeared on  International Christian Concern .
summary_zh: 11月6日，一名名叫阿贾克·马比奥尔（Ajak Mabior）的18岁基督徒女孩在南苏丹琼莱州因拒绝接受家人包办的强迫婚姻而被殴打致死。她本应嫁给一位年长的穆斯林男子——由于她的基督教信仰以及不愿意被强迫结婚，她反对这桩婚事。此后……   这篇题为《因拒绝强迫婚姻而被杀害的女孩》的文章  最初发表在  国际基督徒关注组织  网站上。
title_zh: 因拒绝强迫婚姻而被杀害的女孩
content: On Nov. 6, an 18-year-old Christian girl named Ajak Mabior was beaten to death in Jonglei, South Sudan, after refusing to enter a forced marriage arranged by her family. She was expected to marry an older Muslim man — a marriage she opposed because of her Christian faith and her unwillingness to be forced into it. After attempting to escape, she was killed by her own brother and cousin. Days later, police in Bor arrested the two men but released them without charges after family members demanded their freedom, arguing that “there was no case” because they were relatives. A Common Problem The killing has raised serious concerns among Christian leaders about the pressure Christian girls face when their faith and personal convictions conflict with family expectations. “When a young girl is killed for refusing a forced marriage, and the killers walk free because they are family, the message is clear: Tradition is stronger than the law, and stronger than the value of a life,” a local pastor said. “Many of our Christian daughters live under this same shadow.” For Christian girls in South Sudan , forced marriages can become a matter of religious persecution when they are pressured to marry outside their faith and abandon their Christian convictions. Those who refuse may face rejection, threats, intimidation, and violence from their own families. Mabior’s death highlights the vulnerability of young Christian women who seek to remain faithful to Christ while facing pressure to submit to marriages that violate their faith and conscience. “The church teaches that every life is precious because it is created in the image of God,” the pastor added. “Yet when a Christian girl refuses a marriage that would bind her against her will, she can be treated as a traitor to the community. We have buried too many who paid that price.” Seeking Justice The authorities’ response has added to the church’s concerns. Police reportedly released the suspects without the consent of the Jonglei State Caretaker Commissioner. The justification that the suspects were relatives raises serious questions about the protection available to Christian girls facing forced marriages and violence. When perpetrators are released without facing justice, vulnerable Christian women are left with little confidence that the authorities will protect their right to practice their faith and make decisions according to their conscience. “We preach freedom in Christ, but our young people still live in fear of the consequences of that freedom,” the pastor said. “If the police and local authorities remain quiet, the church becomes the only place left where these girls and boys can find a voice. We need courage to speak, and we need the wider Body of Christ to stand with us.” Mabior’s case raises concerns about forced interfaith marriages, religious pressure, and violence against young Christian women in South Sudan. “We call on the wider Body of Christ to pray for Ajak’s justice, and for the protection of Christian girls facing forced marriages because of their faith,” an International Christian Concern (ICC) staffer said. “Pray that the church will have the courage to speak against religious coercion and violence, and that the authorities will uphold the law and protect vulnerable believers.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . The post The Girl They Killed for Refusing a Forced Marriage first appeared on International Christian Concern .
content_zh:
11月6日,一名名叫Ajak Mabior的18岁基督教女孩在南苏丹琼格莱州因拒绝参加家庭安排的强迫婚姻而被殴打致死。 她被期望嫁给一个年长的穆斯林男子——她反对这种婚姻,因为她的基督教信仰以及她不愿意被迫加入. 在试图逃跑后,她被自己的哥哥和表妹杀死.

几天后,Bor的警察逮捕了这两名男子,但在家属要求他们自由后,在没有指控的情况下将他们释放,他们辩称“没有案件”,因为他们是亲属。 常见问题 杀害事件引起了基督教领袖的严重关切,基督教女孩在信仰和个人信念与家庭期望相冲突时面临压力。

“当一名年轻女孩因拒绝强迫婚姻而被杀害,而杀人者因是家人而自由行动时,信息是明确的:传统比法律更强大,比生命的价值更强大。” 一位当地牧师说。

“我们许多基督教女儿生活在这种阴影下。” 对于南苏丹的基督教女孩来说,当她们被迫在信仰之外结婚并放弃基督教信仰时,强迫婚姻就可能成为宗教迫害的问题。 拒绝者可能面临自己家庭的排斥、威胁、恐吓和暴力。

Mabior的死亡凸显了基督教青年妇女的脆弱性,她们试图保持对基督的忠诚,同时面临压力,迫使她们向违反其信仰和良心的婚姻屈服。 牧师补充说,“教会教导每一条生命都是宝贵的,因为它是以上帝的形象创造的。”

“当一个基督教女孩拒绝违背她意愿而束缚她的婚姻时,她可以被当作一个叛徒对待。 我们埋葬了太多付出这一代价的人。” 寻求正义 当局的反应增加了教会的关注。 据报告,警方未经琼格莱州看守专员同意释放了嫌疑人。

关于嫌疑人是亲属的理由,令人对面临强迫婚姻和暴力的基督教女孩获得的保护提出严重问题。 当肇事者在没有受到法律制裁的情况下被释放时,脆弱的基督教妇女对当局将保护其信仰和根据其良心作出决定的权利缺乏信心。

牧师说,“我们在基督中宣扬自由,但我们的年轻人仍然生活在对这种自由的后果的恐惧之中。” “如果警察和地方当局保持安静,教堂就成了这些女孩和男孩能够发表意见的唯一地方。

我们需要勇气说话,我们需要更广泛的基督与我们站在一起。” Mabior案引起了人们对南苏丹境内强迫不同信仰间婚姻、宗教压力以及针对基督教青年妇女的暴力的关注。

“我们呼吁广大的基督机构为阿贾克的正义祈祷,并保护因信仰而面临强迫婚姻的基督教女孩。” 一位国际基督教关注组织的工作人员说。

“祈祷教会有勇气反对宗教胁迫和暴力,并祈祷当局将维护法律,保护脆弱的信徒。” 阅读更多新闻, 请给我们发电子邮件 支持电算中心在世界各地的工作,

title_zh: 随着马来西亚压制良心自由，绝望和恐惧与日俱增
content: A wave of viral social media videos featuring Malaysian citizens publicly declaring their departure from state-sanctioned Sunni Islam has cast a harsh spotlight on the severe lack of religious freedom in the Southeast Asian nation. While state authorities have scrambled to investigate and suppress the footage, international religious freedom advocates warn that the phenomenon highlights a much deeper, systemic crisis: the complete criminalization of apostasy for ethnic Malays and the intense persecution faced by those who desire to follow other faiths, including Christianity. Under Article 160 of the Constitution of Malaysia, all ethnic Malays are legally defined as Muslims. This constitutional binding leaves no legal avenue for a Malay individual to officially change their religion. For those who experience a personal crisis of faith or choose to embrace Christianity, the path forward is fraught with state-sponsored surveillance, social ostracism, and severe legal penalties. Central to this machinery of suppression is the powerful federal agency JAKIM (Department of Islamic Development Malaysia) and state-level enforcers like JAIS (Selangor Islamic Religious Department). Together, they operate a rigid, dual-track legal system where Shariah courts hold near-absolute jurisdiction over Muslims. Requests by individuals to officially exit Islam are systematically rejected. Instead of granting freedom of conscience, JAIS and other state bodies actively weaponize mandatory detention in state-run Islamic rehabilitation centers (pusat pemurnian akidah). These centers function as forced re-education camps. Converts who are caught or who attempt to petition the courts for apostasy are routinely sentenced to months of involuntary confinement. Inside, they are subjected to intense psychological pressure, isolation, and compulsory doctrinal lectures designed to break their resolve and force a recantation. Recently, JAIS publicized a court-ordered Istitabah (forced repentance ritual) for a social media figure, signaling that the state will use its full administrative weight to enforce religious compliance. Recent landmark legal battles from 2025 and 2026 expose a devastating reality: born-Muslims face a structural wall of total rejections. In an Oct. 2, 2025 ruling, the Federal Court — Malaysia’s highest civil judiciary — completely shut down a final appeal from a 47-year-old Christian convert who spent years fighting the Shariah court system just to return to his original faith following a divorce. The apex court reaffirmed that civil courts have zero jurisdiction to override Shariah rejections, leaving the believer legally trapped. Similarly, on Jan. 6, 2025, a Selangor woman who was unilaterally converted to Islam as a child saw her final legal challenge collapse at the Federal Court, cementing the precedent that her state identity card (MyKad) must permanently brand her as a Muslim. Even elderly believers who have secretly practiced their faith for decades are being hunted through bureaucracy. In June 2026, a 58-year-old mother filed a prominent judicial review against the National Registration Department (JPN) after they flatly refused to remove the “Islam” label from her identification card — despite her having formally converted out of Islam via a deed poll more than 30 years ago. JPN continues to trap her under state custody, demanding a clearance letter from the Shariah court that officials refuse to grant. The statistics highlight how tightly the trap is wound. Historical data shows that out of 863 formal applications submitted nationwide to leave Islam during a 10-year period, only 168 were granted. Legal analysts emphasize that nearly 100% of those rare exceptions were administrative clerical corrections in East Malaysia — such as a Jan. 7 Kota Kinabalu High Court ruling where a father and three children successfully proved they were raised Christian and that an NRD officer had made a data-entry error. 马来西亚民众公开宣布脱离受国家批准的逊尼派伊斯兰教,

虽然州当局纷纷调查并压制了这些镜头,但国际宗教自由倡导者警告说,这一现象凸显出一个更深层次的系统性危机:完全将叛教行为定为马来人的罪行,以及那些想追随其他信仰,包括基督教的人所面临的严重迫害.

根据"马来西亚宪法"第160条,所有马来民族在法律上被定义为穆斯林. 这个宪法约束给马来人没有合法途径可以正式改变他们的宗教.

对于经历个人信仰危机或选择信奉基督教的人来说,前进的道路充满了国家赞助的监视、社会排斥和严厉的法律惩罚。 这一镇压机制的核心是强大的联邦机构JAKIM(马来西亚伊斯兰发展部)和州一级的执行者,如JAIS(Selangor伊斯兰宗教部)。

它们共同实行僵硬的双轨法律制度,教法法院对穆斯林拥有几乎绝对的管辖权。 个人正式退出伊斯兰教的要求遭到系统的拒绝。 JAIS和其他国家机构没有给予良心自由,而是将强制拘留在国营伊斯兰康复中心(pusat pemournian akidah)的武器化。

这些中心作为强迫再教育营运作。 被捕或试图向法院申请叛教的皈依者通常被判处几个月的非自愿监禁。 在内部,他们受到强烈的心理压力、孤立和强制性的理论讲座,目的是打破他们的决心并强迫他们退位。

最近,JAIS为一名社交媒体人物公布了法院下令的Istitabah(强制忏悔仪式),表明国家将利用其全部行政权重强制宗教服从。 最近2025年和2026年的划时代的法律战暴露出一个毁灭性的现实:生来-穆斯林面临一堵彻底拒绝的结构性墙. 在十月一个。

2,2025 年的裁决,联邦法院——马来西亚最高民事司法机构——彻底关闭了对一位47岁的基督教皈依者的最后上诉,这位基督教皈依者花了多年与教法法院系统抗争,只是在离婚后恢复了原来的信仰. 最高法院重申,民事法院对推翻伊斯兰教法的拒绝没有管辖权,使信仰者在法律上受困。

同样,在2025年1月6日,一名Selangor妇女从小单方面皈依伊斯兰教,目睹她在联邦法院的最后法律质疑崩溃,巩固了她的州身份证(MyKad)必须永久地将她贴上穆斯林标签的先例。 即使是几十年来秘密地信奉信仰的老信徒,也正被官僚主义所追捕.

2026年6月,一名58岁的母亲向国家登记局提出了重要的司法审查,因为尽管她通过30多年前的一次契约民意测验正式改信了伊斯兰教,但他们坚决拒绝从身份证上取出“伊斯兰”的标签。

JPN继续将她置于国家监管之下,要求教法法院出具官员拒绝批准的许可信。 统计数字突出表明,陷阱的伤势十分严重。 历史数据表明,在全国提交的863份正式申请中,只有168份获得批准。

title_zh: 你不能就说耶稣爱我吗？
content: “Hold the lettuce.” The simple sentence, perhaps stated more frequently than we might hope, captures a crucial hallmark that predominates in the thinking of many. At a recent lunch with a friend, I saw this firsthand. For my friend, it wasn’t just the lettuce. The instructions he gave restrained the cook from adding anything remotely vegetable-like to the hamburger. Notwithstanding my jibe, my friend held fast to his decision. He was the one ordering. And he expected (rightly so!) to be served what he desired. After all, the customer is king. This cluster of expectations animates the modern marketplace. We want products tailored to our specific needs. We seek out services that let us pay only for what we want. We get frustrated when we take the car to a mechanic who not only fixes the problem we knew about but also takes the liberty of repairing other problems (and charging liberally for them). In short, we want (and expect) to be served according to our preferences and felt needs. Innocuous enough when it comes to the morsels on our plates, the reign of personal preferences involves more serious implications when it extends over the rest of life. And in the life of faith, the consequences are serious indeed. For preference-driven faith will, in the end, produce a Christless Christianity. Have It Your Way What do we hope for when we join the church for worship? Parsing motives presents no easy project, especially if there are children in tow or responsibilities for some aspect of the service or fellowship. Few of us have the personal or cognitive space to search out the depths of our hearts en route to the Sunday morning service. But the way home often presents opportunities to interrogate those hidden recesses. The questions we pose shed light on what is in our hearts: “How did you like the sermon this morning?” “Didn’t the worship team nail it today?” We tend to ask not about a confrontation with gospel truth but about measures of personal satisfaction. If our questions begin illuminating this tendency, the answers we give put our motives on clear display: “I thought the pastor did a great job! I really liked . . .” or “Ya know, I just wasn’t feeling it this morning; the sermon didn’t really speak to me.” “Yes, the worship was great!” or “I thought the team was a bit off. Did you hear them mess up on that one song?” So often, whether at the sandwich shop or on the way home from church, preference-driven language bubbles out of our mouths like boiling water from an unwatched pot. For many, our post-service concerns center far too frequently on how well certain aspects of the service met our felt needs. What did I gain from the sermon? Did I enjoy the music? Service to the ascendant self predominates. We reflect on the worship gathering in a manner unsettlingly similar to how we might reflect on a hamburger: It was decent, but I’ve had better elsewhere. I think they overdid the mayonnaise, and I would have preferred sesame rather than a brioche bun. Whether we want to admit it or not, our expectations of being served as we please spill into our perceived relationship to the church’s gathered worship. Those same expectations shape how we approach our Lord. We tend naturally, in our sin, to want merely an affirming savior. We like to hear that Jesus loves sinners so much that he died to win them, for hearing this affirms that our need for forgiveness has been met. We like to hear that his love for his sheep never falters, for hearing this quells the fear that perhaps our snide words or dubious choices or the train wreck of our inner thoughts might put our hope in jeopardy. We like to hear how our Lord railed against the hypocrisy and legalism of the Pharisees, for hearing this makes us smile inwardly, pleased that we are not so pretentious and uptight. Messages such as these leave us content, unruffled, ready to carry on with life as normal, affirmed in our preferred way of life by a (truncated) gospel that accomplishes little b
content_zh:
“抓住生菜。” 这个简单的句子,也许比我们所希望的更频繁地说,抓住了在许多人的思想中占主导地位的关键标志。 最近和一个朋友共进午餐时 我亲眼看到的 对我的朋友来说, 他给厨师的指示 禁止在汉堡里添加任何类似蔬菜的东西

我的朋友坚持他的决定 是他订的 他希望自己所欲达到的, 毕竟客为王. 这一组期望激发出现代市场。 我们需要适合我们具体需要的产品。 我们寻求服务,让我们只为所欲为。

我们感到沮丧的是,我们把车送到一个技工那里,他不仅解决了我们所知道的问题,而且还自由地修复了其他问题(并且对这些问题收取宽松的费用)。 简言之,我们希望(并期望)根据我们的喜好和感受到的需要得到服务。

谈到我们盘子里的泥潭时,个人偏好的统治,如果延续到余生,就会产生更严重的影响。 在信仰的生活中,后果确实很严重。 因为受偏好驱使的信仰,最终会产生出一种没有基督的基督教. 我们加入教堂做礼拜时希望什么?

分析动机并非易事,特别是如果有儿童被拖走或承担某些方面的服务或研究金责任。 我们当中很少有人拥有个人或认知空间,在前往周日早间礼拜的路上去探寻内心深处. 但回家的方式往往为审讯那些隐蔽的休庭提供了机会。

我们提出的问题揭示了我们心中的心事,“你今天早上喜欢讲道吗?” 我们往往不问与福音真相的对抗,而是问个人满意的措施。 如果我们的问题开始说明这一趋势,我们给出的答案清楚地显示了我们的动机:“我认为牧师做了一件伟大的工作!

我真的很喜欢. . . . . . . . . “是的,崇拜是伟大的!”或“我认为队伍有点偏差。 你听到他们把那首歌弄乱了吗?” 所以,无论是在三明治店,还是在从教堂回家的路上,偏好驱动的语言泡从我们嘴里喷出,就像从一个无人观察的锅中取出沸水来.

对许多人来说,我们的服务后关切过于频繁地集中在服务的某些方面在多大程度上满足了我们的需要。 我从布道中得到什么? 我很喜欢音乐吗? 服务于上层的自我占主导地位。 我们以令人不安的方式思考礼拜聚会, 但我在别处生活得更好。

我觉得他们做了蛋黄酱, 我更喜欢芝麻,而不是布洛克包。 无论我们是否愿意承认这一点,我们期望得到服务,因为我们希望与教会所聚集的礼拜的感同身受。 同样的期望决定了我们如何接近我们的主。 我们的罪孽中,自然而然地只想要一个坚定的救世主。

我们喜欢听到耶稣如此地爱罪人,以至于他为了赢得他们的胜利而去死,因为听到这个消息,肯定了我们对宽恕的需要已经得到满足了. 我们想听到,他对他的羊的爱从未动摇,因为听到这种平息的恐惧,也许我们的暗语或可疑的选择,或者我们内心思想的火车残骸会使我们的希望陷入危险.

我们想听听我们的主如何反对法利赛人的虚伪和法西斯主义,因为听到这使我们对内微笑,很高兴我们没有这么自大和紧张。 这样的讯息给我们留下了内容,没有磨损,准备继续正常生活,在我们所偏爱的生活方式中,用一个(经磨练的)福音来证实,这些福音成就不大。

title_zh: 您的休息习惯揭示了您的内心
content: “Hey, honey, you’re not going to be able to sleep tonight if you don’t start shutting things down soon!” After 36 years of marriage, my husband knows me well. He’s absolutely right, but I still sometimes want to keep pushing until bedtime. The way of wisdom is to stop consciously, set the work aside, and engage in the repetitive, mundane wind-down of the day. The work will still be there tomorrow, and I can trust God for new mercies to finish when morning comes (Lamentations 3:22–23). Our habits of rest reveal what we trust. While our need for sleep, recreation, and downtime weighs on our very physical, very finite bodies, we often resist submitting to our limitations. Substituting entertainment for true rest, we become passive consumers of endlessly streaming content that devours our time. Paradoxically, we crave rest and engage in ceaseless striving after things we hope will satisfy the desires of our heart. This is an ongoing battle for me, and I know I’m not alone. Our society values activity and busyness. We spend our hours and days going and doing, always with one eye on the clock. We reward tireless resilience with job promotions and earnest admiration. In our fervor for achievement, we may forget that rest is necessary for quality work to continue — and that rest can teach our hearts to trust God. Rest Reveals the Heart Psalm 127:1–2 is a reminder for our caffeinated and sleep-deprived souls that progress depends not solely on the work of our own hands but on God’s gracious provision: Unless the L ORD builds the house, those who build it labor in vain. Unless the L ORD watches over the city, the watchman stays awake in vain. It is in vain that you rise up early and go late to rest, eating the bread of anxious toil; for he gives to his beloved sleep. Note that the psalmist illustrates a right and a wrong way to work. He makes three important points for the restless. 1. The Lord builds the house. God builds the ministry, the family, and the career. We work in cooperation with the Lord, and he watches over us and our work. The point is not that we shouldn’t work heartily at whatever we do (Colossians 3:23). Rather, our security is found in God, not in our efforts. Knowing our frame, remembering that we are dust, God commands us to observe regular patterns of rest, not only for our physical health but also as an acknowledgment of our dependence upon him (Psalm 103:14). 2. The Lord watches over the city. Whether we’re closing our eyes or closing our laptop and office door at the end of the day, when we leave the results of our work in God’s hands, we demonstrate trust in him. “He who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep,” the psalmist writes (Psalm 121:4). God is your keeper, too. Entrusting our work to the Lord prevents it from becoming an idol. In our glad contemplation of work well done, we remember that he is both giver and gift. Our work is evidence of his power and goodness. 3. The Lord gives sleep to his beloved. Anyone who has spent a night sleepless from worry knows our bodies are not designed to run on anxious adrenaline. Insomnia has many causes and may not indicate a spiritual problem, but God often uses physical symptoms to reveal our spiritual condition. A steady diet of “the bread of anxious toil” (Psalm 127:2) starves us of what we need most: the ability to rest in God. When we rest, we accept our God-given limits. We hand the controls over to him. We lay aside our disordered loves, and we choose to believe the Father’s delight in Christ is also for us, his treasured children: “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased” (Matthew 3:17). Because it can feel entirely unnatural, we may need to approach rest as a learned behavior, a habit of holiness, a spiritual discipline that we “put on” in the same way Paul exhorted the Colossians to clothe themselves with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience (Colossians 3:12). Such discipline is worth the effort; when we rest, we proclaim
content_zh:
“嘿,亲爱的,你今晚不能睡觉了, 经过36年的婚姻,我丈夫很了解我. 他说得对, 但我还是想继续推到睡觉。 智慧之道在于自觉停止,把工作搁置一边,从事日常的反复,无常的风化.

工作明天仍然会到来,我可以相信上帝会在早晨完成新的慈悲(3:22-23号纪念日)。 我们的休息习惯揭示了我们所信任的东西。 虽然我们对睡眠、娱乐和休息时间的需求影响着我们身体,非常有限的身体,但我们常常不愿屈从于我们的局限性。

以娱乐来代替真正的休息, 我们成为被动的消费者 无限流畅的内容 吞噬我们的时间。 矛盾的是,我们渴望休息,在我们希望能够满足我们内心愿望的事情之后,进行不懈的努力。 这是一场持续的斗争, 我们的社会重视活动和繁忙。

我们花我们的时间和时间去和做, 总是一眼钟。 我们以工作晋升和真诚的钦佩来奖励不懈的韧性。 在我们追求成就的热情中,我们可能忘记,为了继续开展高质量的工作,休息是必要的——休息可以教导我们相信上帝。

安息吧 127:1–2 提醒我们吃咖啡和失眠的灵魂 进步不仅取决于我们自己的工作 也取决于上帝的恩赐: 除非LORD建造房子,否则建造房子的人会白费力气。 除非LORD监视整个城市,否则守望者会白白地保持清醒.

你早起,晚去休息,吃急劳的面包,那是徒劳的。他使他所爱的睡眠。 请注意,诗人表明了一种正确和错误的工作方式。 他为不安的人提出了三个重要点. 1. 主建房屋。 神造部,家人,事业.

我们与上帝合作,他监视着我们和我们的工作。 关键不是我们不应该在做任何事情时勤奋工作(3:23)。 相反,我们的安全在于上帝,而不是我们的努力。

上帝知道我们的框架,记得我们是尘土,命令我们观察正常的休息模式,这不仅是为了我们的身体健康,也是为了承认我们对他的依赖(第103:14段)。 2. 主观城.

无论是闭眼还是关闭手提电脑和办公门, " 保住以色列的人既不睡也不睡, " 诗人写道(第121:4段)。 上帝也是你的守护者 将我们的工作托付给主,防止它成为偶像.

在我们愉快地看待出色的工作时,我们记得,他既是馈赠者,也是天赋。 我们的工作证明了他的力量和善良。 3,主让他的爱人睡觉. 任何因忧愁而睡不着夜的人都知道 我们的身体不是想靠焦虑的肾上腺素运行的

失眠有很多原因,可能没有表明精神问题,但上帝经常使用身体症状来揭示我们的精神状况. 稳定的“焦急劳累的面包”(第127:2段)使我们无法满足我们最需要的:在上帝中安息的能力。 当我们休息时,我们接受上帝赐予我们的限制。 我们把控制权交给他

我们抛下我们无序的爱,我们选择相信父亲对基督的喜悦也是对我们,他珍贵的孩子们:“这是我所爱的儿子,我很高兴与他们在一起”(Matthew 3:17)。

由于它会感到完全不自然,我们可能需要将休息视为一种有学问的行为,一种圣洁的习惯,一种我们以同样方式“寄托”的精神纪律,保罗劝说科洛斯人以慈悲、善良、谦逊、温柔和耐心为己任(科洛斯人3:12)。 这种纪律值得我们努力;当我们休息时,我们宣布

title_zh: 我们对耶稣的眼泪有什么误解
content: Audio Transcript “Jesus wept” (John 11:35). It’s the shortest verse in the Bible. We read it together in the Navigators Bible Reading Plan yesterday. But it’s so brief we can pass it too quickly. Maybe we pass over it because we think we know what it means. Jesus’s friend Lazarus died. Jesus wept because his friend was gone. But what if we got that wrong? Or, what if we mistakenly thought his emotions were simple when they were complex? What if Jesus wept not simply in the loss of death but from a frustration with the living? Today on Ask Pastor John: what we get wrong about the tears of Jesus. Henry, a listener, writes in with a timely question on John 11:35. “Pastor John, thank you for taking my question today. I’d like to ask you about John 11:35. Why do you think Jesus wept at the tomb of Lazarus? One way to read this account is that he’s simply sharing in Mary and Martha’s sorrows over his death. But I wonder if something deeper is going on here. Jesus already planned to raise Lazarus, and he even told his disciples he was going to do it in John 11:11–15. “So, my questions are these two: First, why does Jesus ask, ‘Where have you laid him?’ Was he simply asking to be taken to the tomb? When they answer, ‘Lord, come and see,’ it’s almost like they still don’t appreciate who he is as the Messiah. And that is my second question: This whole event leaves me wondering if this weeping is more like Jesus’s weeping over Jerusalem in Luke 19:41 — weeping because he is heartbroken over the city’s unbelief. Is it a stretch to connect these two moments? Is Jesus grieving the dead Lazarus? Or is he grieving the unbelief of the living?” I doubt that any of Jesus’s emotions were simple. I think they were always complex. We finite creatures have emotions that respond to one or two, maybe three, happy or painful aspects of a situation. So, we may feel sorrow and joy mingled because, say, a very old saint has just gone to be with the Lord, and we will miss him, and yet we’re so happy for him. But Jesus could see every angle, every imaginable aspect of a situation, some of which called for very different emotions. So, I doubt that he ever had a simple emotion. For example, in Mark 3:1–5, there’s this man with a withered hand in the synagogue, and the people are watching to see if Jesus would heal him so that they could accuse Jesus. Can you imagine? They don’t give a hoot about this man’s pain. All they want is to accuse Jesus if he heals him. And in verse 5, it says, “He looked around at them with anger, grieved at their hardness of heart.” And that’s what I mean by complex emotions: anger and grief perfectly mingled in the sinless heart of Jesus. Another example would be that he looked on unbelieving Jerusalem and wept: “Would that you, even you, had known on this day the things that make for peace! But now they are hidden from your eyes” (Luke 19:42). But in Luke 10:21, it says Jesus “rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, ‘I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden these things from the wise and understanding and revealed them to little children; yes, Father, for such was your gracious will.’” He could weep and rejoice over the wise and bitter providence of God. So, we come to John 11 and the death of Lazarus. And I think Henry, who’s sending us this question, is right when he says Jesus’s tears in John 11 aren’t just about sharing our human grief — that maybe he is genuinely mourning their spiritual blindness. Yes, and I’m going to say not just mourning — he’s indignant. The story begins in John 11:1–6 with Mary and Martha sending words to Jesus that their brother Lazarus is very sick. Jesus waits two more days before going and intentionally lets Lazarus die. He says in John 11:14–15, “Lazarus has died, and for your sake I am glad that I was not there, so that you may believe.” That’s an amazing statement: “I let him die for the sake of your faith.” “They needed to see the glory of Jesus more than they needed the

" 耶稣哭泣 " (John 11:35)。 这是圣经中最短的一首诗。 我们昨天一起在《航海家圣经阅读计划》上读到的。 但时间太短了, 也许我们通过它,因为我们认为 我们知道它意味着什么。 耶稣的朋友拉扎鲁斯去世. 耶稣因为朋友不在而哭泣. 但如果我们搞错了呢?

或者,如果我们错误地认为 他的情绪是简单的 当它们是复杂的? 如果耶稣不仅在死亡中哭泣,而且在对活人的挫折中哭泣呢? 今天在"问约翰牧师"(Pastor John):我们对于耶稣的眼泪有什么错误. 亨利是一位听众,他及时写下约翰11:35的问题. “约翰神父,谢谢你今天接受我的问题。

我想问你约翰11点35分的事。 你觉得耶稣为什么在拉扎鲁斯的坟墓上哭泣? 他只是分享玛丽和玛莎对死亡的悲伤。 但我想知道这里是否发生了更深层的事情。 耶稣已经计划要抚养拉撒路人,他甚至告诉门徒他要在约翰11:11–15中完成.

我问的是这两个问题:首先,耶稣为什么问:你们把他放哪儿了? 他只是要求被带去坟墓吗? 当他们回答“主啊,快来看”时,

这是我第二个问题: 这整起事件让我怀疑这起哭泣事件是否更像是耶稣在路加19:41为耶路撒冷所哭泣, 连接这两个瞬间是不是很长一段时间? 耶稣在哀悼死去的拉撒路吗? 还是他痛恨众生的不信呢?” 我怀疑耶稣的任何情绪都很简单。

我觉得他们总是很复杂 我们有限的生物的情绪 反应了一两个, 也许三个,快乐或痛苦的方面 一个情况。 因此,我们可能感到悲伤和欢乐,因为,比如说,一个非常老的圣人刚刚与上帝在一起,我们将怀念他,然而,我们为他感到如此的高兴。

但是,耶稣可以看到每个角度,一个局势的每一个可想象的方面,有些需要非常不同的情绪. 所以我怀疑他有没有过简单的情绪 例如,在Mark 3:1–5中,有一个人手在犹太会堂里枯萎了,人们正在观察耶稣能否治愈他,以便他们指控耶稣。 你能想象吗?

他们不关心这个人的痛苦。 他们只想指控耶稣 如果他治愈他。 在第5节中,他说:他愤怒地注视着他们,他们为自己的坚硬而悲伤。 这就是复杂的情感的含义:愤怒和悲伤完全混入了耶稣的无罪之心。

另一个例子是,他注视着不信的耶路撒冷并哭道:"但愿你,甚至你,在今天知道什么是和平的! 但是现在它们被隐藏在你的眼睛之外”(19:42)。

但在"路加福音"第10:21节中说:"耶稣在圣灵中欢喜,并且说:我感谢你,天地之主,你把这些东西隐藏在智者与明者之间,并把它启示给小孩子;是的,神父,这是你的仁慈的意志". 他可以为上帝的睿智和痛苦的上帝而哭泣和欢乐。 所以,我们来到约翰11号 和拉撒路的死亡。

我认为亨利(Henry)向我们提出这个问题, 他说耶稣在约翰十一世的眼泪并不只是分享人类的悲痛, 我不仅要表示哀悼, 故事从约翰11:1–6开始,由玛丽和玛莎向耶稣发送了他们的兄弟拉扎鲁斯病得很重的话.

耶稣再等两天,然后故意让拉撒路死去. 他在"约翰·11:14-15"一文中说:"拉撒路已经去世了,为了你,我很高兴我没有在场,以便你相信". 这是一个惊人的说法:“我让他为了你的信仰而死。 ” 他们需要看到耶稣的光荣 而不是他们需要的

title_zh: 你就不能帮我吗?
content: Several times now, I have been out in creation with unbelievers, speaking to them of eternal matters, and, passing by a dying branch at the base of a tree, I have picked it up and said, “This is your life apart from Christ.” Speaking about their souls, Jesus’s illustration is irresistible. The conversation goes something like this: Jesus gives us this illustration. He looks you in the eye and says that he is the tree (to augment the illustration slightly), and you are the branch. Look up and see the branches above us, beautiful leaves waving, healthy in their vibrant greens, bearing evidence of life. And then there is this branch. Dry. Leafless. Withered. Why? Because it is detached from the source of its life. Cut off from the one it was made to have communion with. And so, it lies here, detached from its purpose and severed from the only thing that can make it flourish. Jesus claims to be man’s source. He claims to be the Tree to whom you belong. In relationship with him, you have life. Apart from him, he teaches, you spend life withering. I usually pause to let the claim have its proper space. I ask what they think of such an assertion. I give them an opportunity to respond. I have often expected indifference or offense, but I have consistently been met with quiet consideration or outright acknowledgment that such an illustration made sense to them. Or at least they would like to hear more. So I go on to wonder aloud with them. What is it like to be a branch fallen from the tree that is, as Jesus says, withering ? Don’t you know? Need we ask? The restlessness, the fatal dryness, the looming death. The reaching out to anything and everything for life — except for the tree standing beside and over us. Him we do not want. Him we can do without. We can make it our own way. The adverb is different, but the end is the same — restless withering, drunken withering, religious, secular, or thoughtless withering . Some overdose on pleasure. Others get high on their own morality. Still others distract themselves from death’s shadow creeping over them with fantasy football and rounds of golf. But for all that, withering. But Jesus himself asserts that he is the Tree. He is the one we were made for; in him alone can we find the life that haunts us in still and sober moments. Be grafted to him through repentance and faith, be attached to him by the Spirit of the living God, have his words live in you, direct you, amaze you, and dead things will come to life. And what will it be on that day, I am compelled to continue, for those dry and fruitless branches who refused life in him? They will be gathered and thrown into the fire and burned as useless things. But Jesus came that you might have otherwise. He told us his mission was to bring life — life abundantly . Imagine the branch grafted to the tree, suddenly infused with life and purpose and the vital sap of God’s own Spirit. We are as branches; the Father, Son, and Spirit are the source of everlasting life. With him, we flourish though all may seem to go poorly. Without him, only sapped wood remains. Would you like to know more about this Jesus? Now, I tell you this to highlight one of many places where the Bible addresses the interiority of man and its solution: God. I want you to see how dangerous the alternative answers found in modern therapeutic culture are to our souls and our churches. It is a scourge, especially to this inward age, not because a therapeutic culture takes distresses of the heart seriously, but because it too often sends branches reaching out for anything but the Tree. Ingrown Toenails The problem comes not from a focus on the inner man. Anyone who says the Bible has little to say about internal battles, demons, depressions, anxieties, doubts, and the despairs of human life should not air his ignorance. The Scriptures abound with stories of the faithful brought into all the perplexities and pains of life in a fallen world. The Psalms, as one profound example, give u
content_zh:
现在,我曾与不信道的人们一起造化他们,他们谈论永恒的事物,我从树的基部走过一个垂死的树枝,我就捡起树枝,说:这是你们除基督外的生活。 说到他们的灵魂,耶稣的插图是不可抗拒的. 谈话是这样的:耶稣给我们这个插图.

他看着你的眼睛,说他是树(稍加插图),你是树枝。 抬头看上面的树枝,美丽的叶子挥舞着, 健康地在生机勃勃的绿色中,有生命的证据。 然后是这个分支。 干,无叶. 废. 为什么? 因为它脱离了生命的来源。

切断了与它 与圣餐。 因此,它躺在这里,脱离了它的目的,从唯一能够使它蓬勃发展的东西中分离出来. 耶稣自称是人类的来源. 他自称是你所属的树 在他的关系,你有生活。 除了他,他还教书,你一辈子都在消磨 我通常会停下来 让权利主张有它的适当空间。

我问他们如何看待这种断言。 我给他们机会作出回应。 我常常期望冷漠或冒犯,但我一直得到静静的考虑或直截了当地承认,这种说明对他们来说是有意义的。 或至少他们想听更多。 所以我继续问起他们

从树上掉下来的树枝是什么感觉,就像耶稣说的,枯萎? 你不知道吗? 需要我们问吗? 不安,致命干燥,濒临死亡. 除了站在我们身旁的树之外,为生命而接触一切和一切。 我们不希望他。 没有他,我们做不了。 我们可以自己想办法

副词是不同的,但结尾是相同的——沉闷不息,醉酒不醒,宗教,世俗,或无思想的沉闷...... 兴奋剂过量 另一些人则以自己的道德为荣。 也有人用幻想足球和高尔夫球, 但对于这一切, 枯萎。 但耶稣自己宣称他是树人.

他是我们被造出来的人;只有他我们才能找到在静静和清醒的时刻困扰我们的生活。 通过忏悔和信仰而受他宠爱,被活神的灵附在他身上,让他的言语活在你身上,引导你,惊叹你,死去的东西将复活.

那天我不得不继续 对那些拒绝他生命的干枯和无果树枝 他们将被集合并投入火中,被烧成无用的东西. 但耶稣来了,你也许有 否则。 他告诉我们,他的使命是带来生命——充满生命。

想象一下树上的树枝, 突然注入生命和目的, 我们如枝条一样;父、子、精神是永恒生命的源泉。 和他在一起,我们蓬勃发展,尽管一切似乎都不好。 没有他,只有树枝残骸。 你想知道更多关于这个耶稣的事吗?

现在,我告诉你,这要强调 圣经涉及人类的内在性及其解决方案的许多地方之一:上帝。 我想让你们看看现代治疗文化中找到的替代答案对我们的灵魂和教会有多危险.

它是一个祸害,特别是在这个内在时代,不是因为治疗文化认真对待心灵的烦恼,而是因为它常常发出枝条去寻求除了树以外的任何东西。 内生脚趾甲 问题不在于关注内心的人。

凡是说"圣经"的人,对于内斗,妖魔,抑郁,焦虑,怀疑,以及人类生活的绝望,都没什么好说的,不应该让他的无知发泄出来. 《圣经》中充满了信众的故事,将堕落世界中生活的迷惑和痛苦带入其中。 "诗经"作为一个深刻的例子,给了你

title: A Maker’s Heart
