So we travelled down to London for an exhibition of the Salmon and […]  The post  Discovering Jewish roots, responding to antisemitism  first appeared on  God Reports .
summary_zh: 作者：查尔斯·加德纳 (Charles Gardner) — 我的妻子琳达 (Linda) 并不了解 20 世纪 70 年代和 80 年代她的雇主的犹太背景。她只知道自己喜欢为他们工作，只是为了听从上帝的呼召，与孩子们一起工作。因此，我们前往伦敦参加鲑鱼展览，并且 [...] 发现犹太根源，回应反犹太主义的帖子首次出现在《上帝报告》上。
title_zh: 探索犹太血统，应对反犹太主义
content: By Charles Gardner — Charles and Linda on their wedding day My wife Linda had no idea of the Jewish background of her employers during the 1970s and 80s. She just knew that she loved working for them and only left to follow God’s call to work with children. So we travelled down to London for an exhibition of the Salmon and Gluckstein dynasty, and the story of how these resilient Jewish families fled violent persecution in Eastern Europe to build what became the largest catering company in the world known as J Lyons & Co. Linda worked there as a home economist from 1977-1984 but it was only much later that she learnt of the Jewish nature of the firm that once literally fed Britain with its teashops and corner houses on every high street, and its products in every home, Linda playing her part through her cooking and marketing skills. A few years later, after graduating from Bible College in Bournemouth, she worked at a prayer and reconciliation centre in Northern Ireland where she was introduced to the importance of the Christian faith’s Jewish roots, as a result of which she took a study tour of Israel to learn more. And on a second trip to the Holy Land ten years later, she got more than she bargained for. At Cana in Galilee, where Jesus turned water into wine at a wedding, Linda was given a vision of her own wedding. And we met on a blind date six months later! Though having Jewish ancestry myself, I grew up knowing nothing about it. But I learnt more later, especially after becoming a Christian in my early twenties, as Linda had done. It helped that I had a Jewish believer as my early mentor, and I became increasingly aware of the significance of our Jewish heritage, about which I now write prolifically. Meanwhile Linda, who has been teaching Christianity in Doncaster area schools for over 30 years, also now teaches about Judaism as it forms the context into which Christ came to us, fulfilling all the laws and promises of the Old Testament. So in both our cases, we were kept in the dark about very important aspects of our lives – until the Lord shone his light on the truth. Which brings me to the Christian Church as a whole, especially in the UK. We have known very little, if anything, of our faith’s Jewish roots or of God’s ongoing purposes for Israel. This needs to change – and fast! For we are surely hurtling towards the Messiah’s Second Coming like a high-speed train, in danger of coming off the rails with the rest of humanity if we fail to get to grips with how we Christians fit into the unfolding picture of global opposition to tiny Israel. What is our role as we watch antisemitism spread across the globe like wildfire? Do we just sit and watch, or write it off as having nothing to do with us, and remain silent? Or do we stand up to be counted as those who refuse to salute the new Nazism that portrays itself as anti-Zionism – a Confessing Church walking the way of the cross for God’s chosen people? My questions come as renewed calls are made for an independent inquiry into antisemitism at the BBC following news that Oscar-winning producer Lucie Kon has won £400,000 in compensation from the broadcaster. Lucie’s career is said to have unravelled after she raised concerns about antisemitism within the BBC, though the latter have not admitted to any fault. This is highly significant as millions of UK Christians are (where Israel is concerned) probably more influenced by what they hear from our national broadcaster than what they read in the Bible. 由查尔斯·加德纳(Charles Gardner)——查尔斯和琳达在他们的婚礼当天 我的妻子琳达对1970年代和80年代雇主的犹太背景一无所知. 她只知道她喜欢为他们工作,只好听从上帝的号召,与孩子们一起工作。

于是我们来到伦敦,为沙门王朝和格勒克斯泰因王朝举办展览, 讲述了这些坚韧的犹太家庭是如何逃离东欧的暴力迫害, 来建造一个被称为J Lyons & Co的世界最大的餐饮公司的故事。

琳达从1977年到1984年作为家庭经济学家在那里工作,但直到很晚,她才得知这家公司的犹太性质,曾经真正地向英国提供每条高街上的茶店和角楼,以及每家每户家中的产品,琳达通过她的烹饪和营销技巧扮演了她的角色.

几年后,她从伯恩茅斯的圣经学院毕业后,在北爱尔兰的一个祈祷与和解中心工作,在那里向她介绍了基督教信仰犹太教根源的重要性,因此她前往以色列学习更多知识. 在十年后的第二次圣地之行中,她得到了比她讨价还价的更多.

在加利利的卡纳,耶稣在婚礼上把水变成了葡萄酒,琳达得到了自己婚礼的愿景. 我们六个月后相识了! 虽然自己有犹太血统,但长大后却一无所知. 但我后来学到更多, 特别是在我20多岁时成为基督徒之后, 就像琳达所做的那样。

这有助于我有一个犹太教信徒作为我的早期导师,我越来越意识到我们的犹太遗产的重要性,我现在以正文写道。

与此同时,琳达在顿卡斯特地区学校教授基督教30多年,现在还教授犹太教,因为它构成了基督来到我们面前的背景,履行了《旧约》的所有法律和承诺。 因此,在我们这两种情况中,我们被蒙在鼓里,谈论着我们生活中非常重要的方面,直到上帝照亮真理。

这让我来到整个基督教会 特别是在英国 我们几乎不知道我们的信仰的犹太根源,或上帝对以色列的持续目的。 这需要改变,

因为如果我们不能把握基督徒如何融入全球反对小以色列的景象, 我们肯定会像高速列车一样, 与人类其他部分一同下火车。 当我们看到像野火一样在全球蔓延的反分裂主义时,我们的作用是什么?

我们只是坐视不理,还是把它写成与我们无关,保持沉默? 或者我们被算作拒绝向将自己描绘成反犹太复国主义的新纳粹主义致敬的人,

我的问题是,在奥斯卡获奖制片人Lucie Kon从广播公司获得40万英镑的赔偿后,英国广播公司再次呼吁独立调查反犹太主义。 Lucie的职业生涯据说在BBC内提出反分裂主义的担忧后破裂,

由于数百万英国基督徒(就以色列而言)受到我们国家广播机构广播的影响,

而今天的查尔斯和琳达(Charles and Linda),上帝的言语告诉我们“安抚”他的古老人民(以赛亚40:1), 有关以色列正在发生的事情的报道经常被传到造成整个国家遭受创伤的恐怖分子身上,

使徒保罗写道,福音应当被宣布为“首先对犹太人,然后对异教徒”。 (罗姆人1:16) 是的,我们必须分享T

summary: By Howard Cooper — Abdul El-Sayed, the Michigan Democrat who became the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate, says he plans to take his oath of office on a Quran when the new Congress convenes in January. El-Sayed, 42, defeated Republican Mike Rogers on November 3, becoming the first Muslim American elected to the […]  The post  New senator from Michigan says he’ll take oath on Quran  first appeared on  God Reports .
summary_zh: 霍华德·库珀 (Howard Cooper) 撰文：密歇根州民主党人阿卜杜勒·赛义德 (Abdul El-Sayed) 成为第一位当选美国参议院的穆斯林，他表示，他计划在一月份新一届国会召开时，在《古兰经》的基础上宣誓就职。 42 岁的埃尔-赛义德于 11 月 3 日击败了共和党人迈克·罗杰斯，成为第一位当选为 […] 的穆斯林美国人。来自密歇根州的新参议员表示，他将在《古兰经》中宣誓。
title_zh: 密歇根州新任参议员表示他将以古兰经宣誓就职
content: By Howard Cooper — Abdul Al-Sayed (wikipedia commons) Abdul El-Sayed, the Michigan Democrat who became the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate, says he plans to take his oath of office on a Quran when the new Congress convenes in January. El-Sayed, 42, defeated Republican Mike Rogers on November 3, becoming the first Muslim American elected to the Senate and the first epidemiologist to serve in the chamber, according to WION News. In an interview with NPR’s Leila Fadel, he said, “I will likely swear on a Quran. Which Quran, we’re not sure.” He pointed to a copy once owned by Thomas Jefferson, which Keith Ellison used when he was sworn in to Congress, and to an old Quran at the University of Michigan that he described as the first in the state. The US Constitution does not require a Bible or any religious text. In practice, senators usually take the formal oath together on the Senate floor, and a Bible comes into play in individual ceremonial swearings-in. El-Sayed hasn’t said whether he’ll use the Quran in the formal proceedings, the ceremony, or both, and that his choice would not alter the wording of the oath. He has also stressed that his oath will be to the U.S. Constitution,  according to IBTimes. He will be sworn in by Vice President JD Vance, a fact El-Sayed has noted with humor. The Blaze reported he called it a “delicious irony” that Vance is constitutionally required to do so. Not everyone is comfortable with the news. The Daily Signal reported that former White House press secretary Sean Spicer said this week that given El-Sayed’s connections and statements, he should undergo a formal background check before receiving classified information. Presumably, Spicer was referring to Al-Sayed’s family connections to the Muslim Brotherhood. For many Christians, the moment raises questions about the role of faith in public life, the long American tradition of religious liberty, and the Judeo-Christian roots of the United States. El-Sayed and his colleagues are scheduled to be sworn in at noon on January 3, 2027. The post New senator from Michigan says he’ll take oath on Quran first appeared on God Reports .
content_zh:
由霍华德·库珀(英语:Howard Cooper)——阿卜杜勒·赛义德(英语:Abdul Al-Sayed (wikipedia communes)),密歇根州民主党人阿卜杜勒·艾尔·赛义德(英语:Abdul El-Sayed)成为美国参议院首位当选的穆斯林议员,他说他计划在1月份新国会召开时,在《古兰经》上宣誓就职.

42岁的赛义德在11月3日击败共和党人迈克·罗杰斯,成为首位当选参议院议员的美国穆斯林,也是首位在议院任职的流行病学家,据WION News报道. 在NPR的Leila Fadel的采访中,他说:“我很可能在《古兰经》上发誓。

这本《古兰经》, 他指曾由托马斯·杰斐逊拥有的一本副本,基思·埃里森在向国会宣誓就职时曾使用过这份副本,指密歇根大学的一本旧《古兰经》,他称之为该州的第一本。 美国宪法并不要求圣经或任何宗教文本.

在实践中,参议员通常在参议院的地板上共同进行正式宣誓,在个别的仪式宣誓中,圣经开始发挥作用. El-Sayed并未表示他是否会在正式诉讼、典礼或两者中使用《古兰经》, 他还强调,根据IBTimes的说法,他将向美国宪法宣誓。

副总统万斯将宣誓就职, 纵火报称万斯是宪法要求的, 不是每个人都对新闻很满意

《每日信号》报道说,前白宫新闻秘书肖恩·斯皮塞尔(Sean Spicer)本周说,鉴于El-Sayed的联系和声明,他在收到机密信息之前,应当接受正式的背景调查。 Spicer大概指的是Al-Sayed与穆斯林兄弟会的家庭联系。

对许多基督徒来说,此时此刻人们质疑信仰在公共生活中的作用,美国长期的宗教自由传统,以及美国的犹太教-基督教根源. 赛义德和他的同事定于2027年1月3日中午宣誓就职. 密歇根州新参议员表示,

summary_zh: 文：查尔斯·加德纳（Charles Gardner）——一位勇敢的也门记者讲述了他在访问以色列后，对以色列的看法发生了翻天覆地的变化，这一说法令联合国感到震惊。他得出的结论是，他被教导要相信的关于犹太人的所有事情都是谎言。鲁艾·艾哈迈德应邀 […]  这篇文章《也门记者访问以色列，观点发生巨大转变》最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
title_zh: 也门记者访问以色列，观点发生戏剧性变化
content: By Charles Gardner — Luai Ahmed speaking at UN (screenshot YouTube) A brave Yemeni journalist has stunned the United Nations with an account of how his view of Israel has dramatically changed following a visit there. And he was led to the conclusion that everything he has been taught to believe about the Jews is a lie. Luai Ahmed was invited to address the assembly by UN Watch, a non-governmental organisation monitoring the international body’s performance, as the UN Human Rights Council gathered to debate racism. He said: “I grew up in Yemen, where the word that we used for black people is ‘abeed’, which quite literally means ‘slaves’. Racism towards black people in my country is horrifying, but it’s not even the most toxic hatred that I was taught. “The first time I ever heard the word ‘Jew’ was in my local mosque when I was nine years old. At the end of Friday prayers, the Imam said: ‘May Allah kill the Jews and the Zionists’. And I responded alongside thousands of Muslims praying beside me: ‘Ameen’.” Luai then continued: “I was taught that Zionism meant killing Arabs, stealing our land, and destroying Islam. Then October 7th came. Hamas terrorists ‘freed Palestine’ by slaughtering 1,200 Israelis and kidnapping more than 200 people, including a one-year-old child. “Almost everyone in my Arab-Muslim circle celebrated. I didn’t. Instead, as a journalist, I decided to visit the so-called Zionist entity, and I was completely shocked to the core by the lack of apartheid and racism that I experienced. “One day, I got an eye infection. At the hospital, the nurses in reception were Jewish. The doctor treating me was Arab. Is there racism in Israel? Of course. There’s racism everywhere. “But Arabs in Israel aren’t called ‘slaves’. They are doctors, engineers, and party leaders. My experience helped me realise that Zionism really just means the Jewish people’s right to a tiny country. Everything I was taught was a lie.” Quite apart from tipping over the tables of woke left-wing ideology spreading its poisonous antisemitic tentacles across the globe, Luai’s testimony also knocks holes into the escalating pressure on the UK to make reparations for the slave trade, which saw plenty of collaborators in the host countries of those who suffered. And of course, the truth that dare not speak its name – that it was Christians like William Wilberforce who put an end to it! Luai is a great inspiration to fellow journalists like me who long for more of our colleagues to stand up and be counted. Thanks also to David Soakell of Christian Friends of Israel’s Watching Over Zion newsletter, November 5, 2026. The post Yemeni journalist visits Israel, dramatically changes views first appeared on God Reports .
content_zh:
一位勇敢的也门记者在联合国(YouTube)讲话时, 而他由此得出了这样的结论:他所学的关于犹太人的一切信仰都是谎言.

Luai Ahmed被联合国观察组织邀请在大会上讲话,该组织是监测国际机构业绩的非政府组织,在联合国人权理事会聚集一堂讨论种族主义问题。 他说:“我成长于也门, 我们用来形容黑人的字眼是“有病”的,

对我国黑人的种族主义令人恐惧, “当我九岁时,我第一次听到`犹太人'这个词是在我的地方清真寺。 星期五祷告结束时,教母说:愿真主杀害犹太教徒和犹太复国主义者。

我与数千名穆斯林一同祈祷: 卢艾接着说:“我被告知犹太复国主义意味着杀害阿拉伯人、偷窃我们的土地并摧毁伊斯兰教。 后于十月七日来. 哈马斯恐怖分子屠杀了1 200名以色列人并绑架了200多人,包括一名一岁儿童,从而“解放了巴勒斯坦”。 “我的阿拉伯-穆斯林圈子里几乎每个人都庆祝。

我没有。 相反,作为一名记者,我决定访问所谓的犹太复国主义实体,我对缺乏种族隔离和种族主义感到完全震惊。 “有一天,我眼睛受到感染。 在医院接待的护士是犹太人. 治疗我的医生是阿拉伯人。 以色列是否存在种族主义? 当然 到处都有种族主义。

“但以色列的阿拉伯人并不被称为奴隶。 他们是医生、工程师和党领袖。 我的经验帮助我意识到犹太复国主义只是意味着犹太人民对一个小国的权利。

我所学的一切都是谎言。” 卢艾的证言不仅在醒目的左翼意识形态席上倾出,在全球散布出有毒的反酋长触角,还打入了英国为奴隶贸易提供赔偿的不断升级的压力的洞口,在那些受苦受难者所在的东道国中,有许多合作者。

当然,那个不敢说出自己名字的真理——是威廉·威尔伯福斯这样的基督徒终结了它! 吕艾对像我这样的记者同事来说是一个巨大的灵感,他们渴望有更多的同事站起起来被统计. 也感谢以色列基督教之友的David Soakell,

title_zh: 蝠鲼带领海洋科学家找到失去的鳍
content: By Mark Ellis — Amber Sparks (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook page) Growing up in Laguna Beach, California, Amber Sparks developed a deep love for the ocean, which led her to study marine science at UC Berkeley and earn a master’s degree at Scripps Institute in San Diego. As co-founder of Blue Latitudes Foundation, she works with industry to find opportunities for conservation, especially with the Rigs-to-Reefs program, when oil drilling platforms are decommissioned. “We work with the oil companies to repurpose certain parts of the platform, retrofit it so that it can remain in place and continue to function as an artificial reef,” she told God Reports. Amber’s work has taken her around the world, with many dive experiences and encounters in the ocean with marine life. But there is one story she will never forget. It happened in the Gulf of Mexico shortly after Amber graduated from Scripps Institute and was invited on a research industry cruise with oil company representatives, scientists, and regulators on a liveaboard vessel. At the Flower Garden National Banks, a marine protected area 200 miles offshore, Amber was excited about her first dive, but slightly nervous. “You don’t know what you’re going to see or what this experience is going to be like,” she recalls. Dropping in (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook) Each diver had to jump off the vessel to get in the water. “We’re all geared up with our snorkel, our buoyancy control device, our wetsuit, and fins are the last thing you put on. So, I put on my fins and I jumped off the side of the boat.” “The second that I hit the water, one of my fins fell off, and I looked down and watched as it slowly descended to the bottom.” Amber glanced over at her dive buddy, and said, “I’m gonna go down. I’m going down.” Normally she would wait for her dive partner and they would go down together, but in this case, she thought, “I can’t (wait). I gotta go get my fin.” So Amber slowly began to descend to the bottom, about 60 feet below the ocean surface. “I felt completely lost. I was in a completely new area. I never dove before, and now I only had one fin.” She realized there were major currents that could have moved her fin in any direction. “I realized I can’t really swim with just one fin. So now not only am I at depth, but I’m handicapped with just one fin, and I started to feel pretty nervous.” It would probably take her 10 minutes to get back the surface, with safety stops. At the moment before panic set in, she looked upward and saw an amazing sight. It was a giant manta ray, with wings extending at least 10 feet. “Its wingspan was double mine. Its arms were out, and it was coming up over the side of a reef. “I’ve never seen a manta ray like this before. It totally took my breath away, it was so magnificent.” Another manta ray (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook page) She noted that manta rays are known in the ocean community to be “majestic, God-connected creatures with an understanding maybe beyond what humans can fully comprehend. They see the world and feel it in another way,” she notes. Mantas have the largest known brain of any fish. Their brains are large in absolute terms and relative to body size, which is also true of elephants, dolphins, and people. Their brains have enlarged areas associated with intelligence, vision, and motor coordination, and some of their brain cells are more like those in birds and mammals than in other fish.(1) As the manta ray drew close to Amber, she had an unusual communication experience. “I felt this sense where it said, ‘I want you to follow me. I’m going to help you find your fin.’ Amber Sparks Amber’s diving partner had just descended next to her, and they both began to swim after the manta. “I was barely making it, following this manta ray across the reef. At this point, I was so excited to see a manta ray. I kind of forgot about being handicapped, and I was just trying to go as fast as I can to keep up with it. Then Amber got the sur

title_zh: 拉尼尔第六届年度约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利系列讲座：圆满成功
content: John Warwick Montgomery While sitting in the John Warwick Montgomery Study Center at the Lanier Library and Study Center in Houston, Texas, awaiting a meeting, I turned to librarian Sharon Cofran and Executive Director Dr. David Fleming and remarked, “John Warwick Montgomery would be very pleased with what Lanier has accomplished on his behalf.” From Montgomery’s framed correspondence with C. S. Lewis and his barrister gowns to the thousands of books that comprise his remarkable personal collection, Lanier has provided the Christian world with a marvelous tribute to one of the great Christian intellectuals of the twentieth and twenty-first centuries. Born in 1931, John Warwick Montgomery (d. 2024) was a distinguished Christian apologist, theologian, attorney, and scholar whose extraordinary career spanned several disciplines. Holding numerous academic degrees, including doctorates in theology, philosophy, and law, Montgomery became internationally recognized for his defense of Christianity through historical evidence, legal reasoning, and philosophical argumentation. His influential books, including History and Christianity , Faith Founded on Fact , and The Shape of the Past , helped establish a rigorous approach to Christian apologetics. Whether lecturing in universities, debating skeptics, or practicing law, Montgomery maintained that Christianity was not merely a matter of subjective belief but a faith grounded in historical reality and rational inquiry. Yet to stop at the library would be to understate Lanier’s remarkable work. The sixth annual John Warwick Montgomery Lecture Series was a tour de force of distinguished thinkers, passionate Christians, and intellectually engaging presentations. More than a commemoration of Montgomery’s life, the gathering represented a continuation of his intellectual legacy: the conviction that Christianity can withstand serious scrutiny and offer compelling answers to life’s most profound questions. Mark Lanier, Nancy Pearcey, Paul Gould, Adam Francisco, and Michael Horton From the opening panel discussion hosted by attorney and philanthropist Mark Lanier to Dr. Paul Gould’s thoughtful presentation on worldviews, followed by attorney Craig Parton’s lecture on jurisprudential apologetics, one theme emerged with unmistakable clarity: Christianity is a reasonable faith. The presentations reflected Montgomery’s own interdisciplinary approach to apologetics: the Christian faith and intellectual inquiry need not be adversaries. Indeed, the Christian tradition has long insisted that faith and reason are complementary avenues in the pursuit of truth. The following day continued this rich intellectual exploration. Professor Nancy Pearcey addressed questions surrounding truth, dismantling various modern ideologies, while Dr. Adam Francisco offered an informative overview of Islamic history and belief, helping participants better understand one of world’s biggest religions. The keynote address by Dr. Michael Horton examined the challenge of reaching those who identify as “spiritual but not religious,” a growing segment of contemporary society. Horton’s presentation underscored the importance of communicating historic Christian truth in a culture increasingly suspicious of religious institutions yet often deeply interested in spiritual meaning. Dr. Michael Horton On Sunday morning, Lanier founder, Mark Lanier, hosted many participants during his Biblical literacy class, where he continued the dialogue with Michael Horton. Taken together, the lectures, discussions, and interviews demonstrated the breadth of Christian scholarship and the continuing relevance of thoughtful apologetics in an age of skepticism, religious pluralism, and cultural uncertainty. As I reflected on the weekend, I was reminded of the Festschrift Christianity for the Tough-Minded , a collection of scholarly essays honoring Montgomery’s life and ministry. 约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利 在德克萨斯州休斯敦拉尼尔图书馆和研究中心的约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利研究中心等待开会时,我找图书管理员沙龙·科夫兰和执行主任戴维·弗莱明博士说:“约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利将非常高兴拉尼尔代表他取得的成就。” 蒙哥马利与C.S.的书信

刘易斯和他的大律师礼服为他杰出的个人收藏的数千本书,为基督教世界向20世纪和21世纪伟大的基督教知识分子之一致敬。 1931年出生于约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利(d.

2024年)是一位杰出的基督教道歉学家,神学家,律师和学者,其非凡的事业跨越多个学科. 蒙哥马利拥有众多学术学位,包括神学,哲学和法学的博士学位,他通过历史证据,法律推理,哲学论证,为基督教辩护而获得国际承认.

他的有影响力的著作,包括历史和基督教、基于事实的信仰、以及过去的造型,帮助确立了对基督教学的严格态度。 无论是在大学里讲课,辩论怀疑论,还是执业法律,蒙哥马利都坚持认为基督教不仅仅是主观信仰的问题,而是建立在历史现实和理性调查基础上的信仰.

然而, 停留在图书馆将会低估拉尼尔的出色工作。 第六届年度约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利讲座系列是由杰出的思想家,充满热情的基督徒,以及智力参与的演讲组成的巡回演出.

这场集会不仅仅是纪念蒙哥马利的一生,它代表着他思想遗产的延续:相信基督教能够经受住严肃的审视,为人生最深刻的问题提供令人信服的答案.

马克·拉尼尔 南希·皮尔西 保罗·古尔德 亚当·弗朗西斯科 迈克尔·霍顿 从律师和慈善家马克·拉尼尔主持的开场小组讨论到保罗·古尔德博士关于世界观的深思熟虑的演讲,然后是克雷格·帕顿律师关于法学理论的演讲,一个主题以明确无误的方式出现: 基督教是一种合理的信仰.

这些介绍反映了蒙哥马利自己对学说采取的跨学科方法:基督教信仰和知识调查不必是对手。 事实上,基督教传统长期以来一直坚持信仰和理性是追求真理的补充途径。 次日继续进行这种丰富的知识探索.

Nancy Pearcey教授谈到了围绕真理的问题,摧毁了各种现代意识形态,而Adam Francisco博士则提供了伊斯兰历史和信仰的翔实概览,帮助与会者更好地理解世界上最大的宗教之一。 由Dr.A.先生作主旨发言。

迈克尔·霍顿研究了帮助那些认为是“精神上但并非宗教上”的当代社会日益扩大的阶层的挑战。 霍顿的演讲强调了在一种对宗教机构越来越怀疑、但往往对精神意义很感兴趣的文化中传播基督教历史真理的重要性。 医生

迈克尔·霍顿 星期天早上,拉尼尔创始人马克·拉尼尔(Mark Lanier)在他的圣经识字课期间接待了许多参与者,在那里他继续与迈克尔·霍顿进行对话.

讲座、讨论和访谈共同显示了基督教奖学金的广度,以及深思熟虑的学说在怀疑主义、宗教多元化和文化不确定性的时代的持续相关性。

summary_zh: 文：查尔斯·加德纳（Charles Gardner）——在第二次世界大战南太平洋的一场海战中，一名日本水兵所在的驱逐舰被美国人击沉，他的大多数战友都淹死了。令人惊奇的是，尽管鱼雷官新谷通晴与其他人一起被卷入波涛之下，随着战舰的沉没，但他却奇迹般地在这场1942年的灾难中幸存下来。（只有18名……）  这篇文章《二战日本战俘在战俘营中找到“自由”》最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
title_zh: 二战日本战俘在战俘营中找到“自由”
content: By Charles Gardner — When a Japanese sailor’s destroyer was sunk by the Americans in a World War II South Pacific battle, most of his companions drowned. Amazingly, even though he was sucked underneath the waves with others as the ship went down, torpedo officer Michiharu Shinya somehow survived this 1942 disaster. (Only 18 of the 200-strong crew did). But he would rather have died at that point as his people had been indoctrinated to believe that it was shameful to be captured. Nevertheless, he was badly wounded but nursed back to health by medics. In time, he was picked up and eventually taken to a Prisoner-of-War camp at Featherston, near Wellington, in New Zealand, where he was to spend the next three years, as Don Stephens records in his inspirational book War and Grace (Evangelical Press, an imprint of 10Publishing). Shinya and his fellow inmates were treated with much kindness (in sharp contrast to the torture often experienced by Allied prisoners at the hands of the Japanese). Being showered with gifts at Christmas, a feast he knew nothing about, seemed especially strange. However, he was determined not to be ‘taken in’ by the Christian teaching offered after some of the prisoners requested spiritual help and a Japanese Bible was made available. That is until he chanced upon an article entitled ‘Sorrow in Victory’ in which the author quoted a ‘Hebrew prophet’ as saying: “Those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength. They shall soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary; they will walk and not be faint.” It made a deep impression on him, and he was determined to find out where it came from. Assuming it was from the Old Testament, he began reading the Bible, starting at Genesis chapter 1. Eventually, to his joy, he discovered that the profound words were from the Book of the prophet Isaiah (chapter 40, verse 31). After flagging somewhat in his search, he found himself hospitalised with malaria when a friend brought him a booklet called The Reason Why explaining the way to salvation. It so happened that the camp’s chaplain, Pastor Hessell Troughton, had been a missionary to Japan and spoke the language. Shinya joined others in his Bible studies and came to know and love Jesus as his Saviour. So much did this “complete freedom” now rule his life that prison had morphed into what he described as “a unique paradise on earth”. He never looked back after that and became convinced that his post-war calling would be in service of his Lord. When he finally returned home, his family were shocked to see him alive for he had been reported as killed in action. He had also given a false name to his captors because of the supposed shame of falling into enemy hands. Shinya subsequently became a pastor and prolific writer and translator following years of theological study both in Tokyo and the US. The Old Testament, he came to believe, demonstrated that sin is “the ultimate problem of mankind” and clearly pointed to Christ as the answer. On seeking to understand why so few Japanese became Christians, he felt it was partly due to their pride borne of believing they were a superior race. As for those three Christmases he spent in New Zealand, author Don Stephens writes: “Of all the gifts he received, the one he valued most was ‘the boundless and deep grace and peace of God in the Lord Jesus Christ’.” The post WWII Japanese POW found ‘freedom’ in camp first appeared on God Reports .
content_zh:
查尔斯·加德纳编著: 当一艘日本水手的驱逐舰在二战南太平洋战役中被美国人击沉时,大部分同伴溺毙. 令人惊奇的是,尽管随着船只的下沉,他与其他人一起被吸在海浪下,但鱼雷军官Michiharu Shinya却不知何故幸免于1942年的灾难。 (200人的船员中只有18人这样做).

但他宁愿死在那个时候,因为他的族人被灌输相信被俘虏是可耻的. 然而,他受了重伤,但被医护人员喂养。

在时间上,他被接了起来,最终被带到新西兰惠灵顿附近的费瑟斯顿(Featherston)的战俘营,在那里他将度过接下来的三年,正如唐·斯蒂芬斯在他的励志书"战争与格蕾丝"(福音出版社,10Publishing的印记)中记载的那样.

信也和同狱囚犯受到很大程度的善待(与盟军囚犯经常在日本人手中遭受的酷刑形成鲜明对比). 在圣诞节用礼物淋浴 一个他一无所知的宴会 看起来特别奇怪

然而,在一些囚犯要求精神帮助和提供日本圣经后,他决心不再接受基督教教义的 " 接纳 " 。 直到他看到一篇题为“为胜利而悲伤”的文章,作者在文章中引用了一位“赫布鲁先知”的话:“那些希望主复活的人。 他们将像鹰一样飞翔,

他们将奔驰,而不会疲倦,他们将走路,而不会晕倒。 这给他留下了深刻的印象,他下定决心要找出它来自何处. 假设它来自旧约,他开始阅读圣经,从创世纪第一章开始. 最终,在他的喜悦中,他发现深刻的文字来自先知以赛亚的经典(第40章第31节).

在搜索中略微浮出水面后,他发现自己患上了疟疾,一位朋友给他带了一本小册子,名为《原因》,解释救世之路。 难民营的牧师Hessell Troughton牧师曾是日本的传教士, 信也加入了其他人的圣经研究,来到了了解和热爱耶稣作为他的救世主.

这种“完全自由”现在统治了他的生活,监狱变成了他所称的“地球上独一无二的天堂”。 他从此之后再也没有回头看,并且确信他的战后召唤将会为他的主服务. 当他最终回家时,家人震惊地看到他活着,因为他被报道为阵亡.

他还给抓捕者取了一个假名,因为被假定是落入敌人手中的耻辱。 在东京和美国多年的神学研究之后,信也后来成为一名牧师和多产作家和翻译。 他逐渐相信,《旧约》表明了罪恶是“人类的最终问题”,并明确指出基督是答案。

在试图理解为什么如此少的日本人成为基督徒时,他感到部分是由于他们的自豪感,因为他们相信他们是优越的种族。

至于他在新西兰度过的三个圣诞节,作者Don Stephens写道:"在他收到的所有礼物中,他最珍视的一件是`上帝在耶稣基督中无限和深厚的恩惠与和平 ' 。 日本战俘在营地发现「自由」,

title_zh: 在西部明星的阴影下：格罗弗·刘易斯、拉里·麦克默特里和文字的胜利
content: With The Grover Lewis Reader: Splendor in the Short Grass and Western Star , the newest biography of Larry McMurtry, in hand, I load my truck and head toward Archer City, Texas, accompanied by my wife, Melanie, and our friend Eliott. Archer City is, of course, McMurtry country, a small Texas town made famous through the literary imagination of one of America’s most celebrated novelists. Having written about McMurtry’s faith—or lack thereof—in a previous article , following an earlier visit to Archer City, I’m returning with a somewhat different interest. This time, my attention turns to Grover Lewis, the gifted journalist, critic, and poet whose life intersected with McMurtry’s during their college years. Lewis’ story, however, begins not with literary achievement but with almost unimaginable tragedy. As a child, he experienced the devastating loss of both parents when his father murdered his mother and was subsequently shot with the same gun, either by his dying wife or another person present. Lewis was only eight years old. It is difficult to imagine a more horrific beginning. Yet rather than allowing that tragedy to become the entirety of his story, Lewis eventually found a voice through literature. Perhaps the cards life dealt him gave him plenty to write about. Or perhaps writing became his way of making sense of a world that had revealed its cruelty far too early. In his autobiographical poem “Hillbilly Song,” Lewis writes: “You asked me once, Ann/Over coffee gone cold with talk/In your mother’s rain-drowsy/House, who they were, how it/Was with them in their breathless/Time in the wilds of years.” For Lewis, those early years were indeed wild. But they were also the soil from which his literary imagination would eventually grow. A Life in Words Born in Texas in 1934, Grover Lewis emerged as a distinctive voice in American journalism, particularly through his cultural criticism and reporting on the rapidly changing landscape of the 1960s and 1970s. He became known for his sharp observations, literary flair, and ability to capture the personalities and contradictions of American culture, even if he occasionally stretched the truth in the telling. His work appeared in prominent publications, including Rolling Stone , where his reporting helped establish his reputation as an insightful, sometimes cutting observer of popular culture. Lewis was more than a journalist, however. He was a poet and literary craftsman, someone who understood that words could do more than convey information. They could illuminate the human condition, expose its contradictions, and perhaps even provide a measure of healing. Grover Lewis (ChatPGT) Continuing “Hillbilly Song,” Lewis ponders: “At last, breathless and dry-mouthed/With private desire in the blue,/Swollen dark, we all lie down together—/My mother, my father, their perishing/Dreams, and I this unborn prisoner son…” There is something haunting about these lines. The dead remain present. The past refuses to disappear. And the poet, even as an adult, seems to wrestle with the circumstances that shaped his entrance into the world. Yet the very act of writing suggests something else: a refusal to remain silent. Two Texans, Two Literary Paths Lewis and Larry McMurtry crossed paths as students at North Texas State College, now the University of North Texas, during the 1950s. Both were young Texans drawn to literature and the possibilities of the written word. Their friendship developed within a shared intellectual environment, one that encouraged reading, conversation, and the pursuit of literary ambitions. Although their careers eventually followed different paths—McMurtry toward novels, screenplays, and literary fame, Lewis toward journalism, poetry, and cultural criticism—they shared an interest in the complexities of American life. content_zh:
与《格罗弗·刘易斯读者:短草中的辉煌与西部之星》,拉里·麦克默特里的最新传记, 手持,我装载我的卡车并前往德克萨斯州阿彻城, 由我的妻子梅兰妮和我们的朋友埃利奥特陪同。 阿彻城当然是麦克默特里国家,一个通过美国最著名的小说家之一的文学想象而成名的德克萨斯小镇.

在之前访问Archer城后, 我对McMurtry的信仰(或缺乏信仰)有一番兴趣, 这一次,我转而关注有天赋的记者、评论家和诗人格罗弗·刘易斯,他在大学时代的生活与麦克默特里的生活交织在一起。

然而,刘易斯的故事并非从文学成就开始,而是从几乎难以想象的悲剧开始. 他从小就经历了父母的惨痛损失,当时他的父亲谋杀了他的母亲,随后被他即将死亡的妻子或在场的其他人用同一把枪射杀。 刘易斯才八岁 很难想象一个更可怕的开端。

然而,刘易斯最终没有让这场悲剧成为他的全部故事,而是通过文学找到了声音. 也许他命中注定的卡片 给他写了很多东西 或写作成为他理解世界的方式, 这个世界已经揭示了它的残酷性,还为时过早。

刘易斯在自传诗“Hillbilly Song”中写道 : “ 你曾经问过我,Ann/Over咖啡随着谈话而变得冷淡,在你妈妈的雨滴/住所里,他们是谁,他们在无气息的年代/在野外时如何。 ” 对刘易斯来说,那些早年的确很狂野. 但它们也是他的文学想象最终会成长的土壤.

1934年出生于德克萨斯州的"言语生活"(A Life in Words Born in Texas),格罗弗·刘易斯(Grover Lewis)成为美国新闻业中一个有特色的代言人,特别是通过他对1960年代和1970年代迅速变化的地貌的文化批评和报道.

他以尖锐的观察,文学的才华,以及能够捕捉美国文化的个性和矛盾而闻名,即使他偶尔在讲述中伸张真理. 他的作品出现在包括滚石公司在内的著名出版物中,他的报道帮助他树立了自己作为有见地,有时剪切流行文化观察者的声誉.

然而,刘易斯不只是一名记者。 他是一位诗人和文学家,一个懂得文字可以比传递信息更有用的人. 它们可以揭示人类的状况,暴露其矛盾,甚至可能提供某种治疗方法。

Grover Lewis (ChatPGT) 继续“Hillbilly Song,” 刘易斯思考道:“最后,无气息和干燥的嘴唇/在蓝色的暗处私欲下,我们都躺在一起——/我的母亲、父亲、他们的死亡/梦想,我这个未出生的囚犯儿子......” 这些台词有些困扰。 死者仍然在场。 过去拒绝消失。

而诗人,即使作为一个成年人,似乎也与塑造他进入世界的环境相搏. 然而,写作本身就暗示了另一种情况:拒绝保持沉默。 两德克萨斯州立大学,两条文学道路刘易斯州立大学和拉里·麦克默特里(英语:Larry McMurtry)在1950年代作为北德克萨斯州立学院,即现在的北德克萨斯大学的学生跨过道路.

两人都是年轻的德克萨斯人,被吸引到文学和写字的可能性. 他们的友谊是在共同的知识环境中发展起来的,这种环境鼓励阅读,对话,追求文学野心.

title: Jewish army doctor turned to Jesus after witnessing patient’s courage
summary: By Charles Gardner — A Jewish army surgeon was amazed by the courage of a young soldier badly wounded in the Battle of Gettysburg during the American Civil War (1861-65). Dr Max Rossvally was forced to amputate both a leg and arm in a bid to save the boy’s life. But it changed his own […]  The post  Jewish army doctor turned to Jesus after witnessing patient’s courage  first appeared on  God Reports .
summary_zh: 文：查尔斯·加德纳（Charles Gardner）——一位犹太籍陆军外科医生对一名年轻士兵的勇气感到惊叹，这名士兵在美国内战（1861-65）的葛底斯堡战役中身受重伤。为了挽救这个男孩的生命，马克斯·罗斯瓦利（Max Rossvally）博士不得不截肢，截掉了他的一条腿和一条胳膊。但这改变了他自己……  这篇题为《犹太军医在目睹病人的勇气后归向耶稣》的文章  最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
title_zh: 犹太军医在目睹病人的勇气后归信耶稣
content: Pastor Peter Colon portraying Major Rossvally in the movie of his story By Charles Gardner — A Jewish army surgeon was amazed by the courage of a young soldier badly wounded in the Battle of Gettysburg during the American Civil War (1861-65). Dr Max Rossvally was forced to amputate both a leg and arm in a bid to save the boy’s life. But it changed his own life. For the 17-year-old Drummer Boy – too young for frontline duty – refused chloroform or brandy to dull the pain. Charlie Coulson chose instead to trust in Jesus, his Lord and Saviour. The doctor – an army major and Orthodox Jew – was understandably stunned by the boy’s bravery, as well as his boldness in declaring his faith in Christ and imploring the officer (whom he knew to be Jewish) to put his own trust in Jesus, since he was also the Jewish Messiah. Max, however, was shaken rigid, and in a great dilemma, as he had always been taught to hate Jesus. For his people had largely rejected him as an ‘impostor’ and false Messiah. Charlie died just days later, apparently more concerned for the doctor’s eternal destiny than for his own painful exit from this life. Ten years later, Max found himself in a barber’s chair in New York once more being urged to trust in Jesus. Having explained the gospel, the barber promised to pray for him and said that, whenever he came in contact with a Jew, he felt it his duty to introduce him to the one who came for “the lost sheep of Israel” (Matthew 10:6). The surgeon subsequently boarded a train for a business meeting in Washington, where a newspaper advertisement drew him to a ‘revival’ service where the preacher echoed the messages he had heard from the barber and the boy soldier, leaving him in tears. He agonised at home in prayer for some time afterwards, struggling most of all with the thought that, if he accepted Christ, he would be going against all the advice and teaching he had known, not to mention the Jewish community as a whole. But he finally became convinced that Jesus was indeed the fulfilment of Old Testament prophecies (in particular, Genesis 49:10, Micah 5:2 and Isaiah 7:14). So he prayed: “O Lord God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. You know I am sincere in this thing. If Jesus Christ is the Son of God, reveal him to me this night, and I will accept him as my Messiah.” A long battle ensued, but his doubts were eventually replaced by joy and happiness as he praised God that he had found the true Shiloh, Ruler of Israel and Emmanuel. He was to pay a high price, however, as do all who follow Christ. His wife walked out on him; his parents disowned him. But he never gave up hope as he constantly prayed and reached out to his family. After 54 days, his wife joined him as a disciple of Jesus and, in time, his daughter also became a believer. But his son disowned him for many years until he was eventually reconciled both with his earthly and heavenly Father. In an extraordinary sequel some 18 months after he came to Christ, Max met up with Mrs Coulson, the mother of his dying young patient all those years earlier on the battlefield. With great joy, he was able to share how her son had set him on the path to a glorious future in Christ, which was to touch lives across the world, including my home county of Yorkshire in England. In fact, he came to live in Leeds to reach out to the Jewish community there and is buried at Lawnswood Cemetery in the city. An Irish friend of mine, Colin Nevin, has visited the grave, which includes an excerpt from one of the doctor’s hymns, I am Coming Soon, and was able to give a copy of Max’s story to a caretaker, so continuing the evangelist’s legacy more than a century after his death in 1892, aged 64. A 54-minute movie – Rossvally: From the Synagogue to the Saviour – has been produced on DVD and can apparently be ordered online. The post Jewish army doctor turned to Jesus after witnessing patient’s courage first appeared on God Reports .
content_zh:
牧师彼得·科隆在他的故事电影"查尔斯·加德纳"(By Charles Gardner)中描绘了罗斯瓦利少校——一位犹太军队外科医生对美国内战期间格底斯堡战役(1861-65)中一名年轻士兵严重受伤的勇气感到惊讶. Max Rossvally医生被迫截肢, 但这改变了他自己的生活。

对于17岁的Drummer Boy — — 年龄太小,无法承担前线任务 — — 拒绝氯仿或白兰地来消磨疼痛。 查理·科尔森选择了信任耶稣,他的主和救世主.

这位医生是一名陆军少校和正统犹太人,对男孩的勇敢以及他大胆地宣布对基督的信仰,恳求军官(他知道是犹太人)相信耶稣是可以理解的,因为他也是犹太弥赛亚。 然而,马克思被动摇僵硬,陷入了巨大的困境,因为他一直被教导要憎恨耶稣.

他的宗族曾否认他是一个 " 骗子 " 和假的弥赛亚。 Charlie在几天后就去世了,显然更关心医生的永恒命运,而不是他自己痛苦地离开这一生。 10年后,马克思发现自己在纽约的理发师座椅上再次被敦促信任耶稣.

在解释了福音之后,理发师答应为他祈祷,并说每当他与一个犹太人接触时,他觉得有义务将他介绍给前来寻找“迷失的以色列羊”的人(Matthew 10:6)。

外科医生随后登上火车在华盛顿举行商务会议,报纸的广告将他引向 " 复活 " 服务,传教士重复了他从理发师和男孩士兵那里听到的信息,使他流泪。

他在家里苦苦地祈祷了一段时间,他首先想到,如果他接受基督,他将反对他所知道的所有建议和教导,更不用说整个犹太社区了。 但他最终确信耶稣确实是"旧约预言"的实现(特别是创世纪49:10,米迦5:2和以赛亚7:14).

他就祈祷说:易卜拉欣、易司哈格、叶尔孤白的主啊! 你知道我对这件事很真诚 如果耶稣基督是上帝之子,那么今晚把他告诉我,我将接受他为我的弥赛亚。” 一场漫长的战斗随之而来,但他的疑虑最终被欢乐和幸福所取代,因为他称赞上帝找到了真正的希洛,以色列统治者和埃马纽埃尔.

但他要付出高昂的代价,跟随基督的所有人一样。 他的妻子抛弃了他;他的父母抛弃了他。 但是,他从未放弃过希望,因为他不断祈祷和联系家人。 在54天后,他的妻子作为耶稣的门徒加入了他,在时间上,他的女儿也成为了信徒.

但他的儿子与他断绝关系多年,直到他最终与他的大地父和天父都和解. 在他来到基督的大约18个月之后的一段非凡续集中,马克思在战场上遇见了那些年前他死去的年轻病人的母亲科尔森夫人.

他怀着极大的喜悦,得以分享她儿子如何使他踏上基督辉煌未来的道路,这就是触摸世界各地的生活,包括我的家乡英格兰约克郡. 事实上,他来到利兹居住,向那里的犹太社区伸出援手,并被埋在城内的草坪林墓地.

我的一个爱尔兰朋友科林·内文参观了这个坟墓,其中包括医生颂歌"I am Coming Soon"的节录,并且能够把马克思的故事复制给看守人,因此在1892年去世后一个多世纪的福音派传承下来,享年64岁.

一部54分钟的电影 — — Rossvally: 从Synagogue到救世主 — 已经在DVD上制作,显然可以在网上订购. 在目睹病人的勇气首次出现在上帝的报告之后,

title_zh: 两只卡车轮胎和一只白鸽教会了我信靠上帝
content: By Mike Shreve — Tent meeting in the 80s Evangelism has been my focus for 55 years, ministering throughout the United States and in 14 other nations. God mercifully saved me during the Jesus Revolution (1970), out of a hippie lifestyle and a passionate, though misguided pursuit of truth through far eastern religious practices (yoga and meditation). Shortly after encountering Jesus and being delivered, along with another brother in the Lord, I began hitchhiking around the country, preaching the Gospel on street corners and college campuses. That developed through the years into ministry in churches, auditoriums, conferences, and tent crusades. Supernatural provision and divine intervention has always carried me, through every phase of this five-and-a-half-decade-long adventure. However, the following story is a classic. For about 25 years I carried big Gospel tents around the country. At the time of this “miracle,” I was transporting a 60’ x 90’ tent from one city to the next in an old, dilapidated bus that kept introducing new challenges to our amateur mechanic skills (putting it mildly). One day, on our way to Tampa, Florida—unfortunately—we hit a large pothole in the road that put a serious dent in the rear left rim on which a large truck tire was mounted. From that point, the inner tube would not retain air, making it necessary to stop every thirty miles or so to fill it up again . . . and again . . . and again . . . making the trip painfully slow. Adding to the problem, the other rear tire was bald, and we had no spare (couldn’t afford one). So, a flat would have brought us to a complete standstill. Sometimes, I think back on those days (when our zeal for the Kingdom outran any wisdom we might have possessed), and I marvel at the many times God took care of us anyway (like the loving heavenly Father that He is). Thousands of pounds of equipment were packed into that groaning, creaking, rusty, decrepit bus — heavy canvas tent sections, metal poles, stakes, platform, and 300 chairs—and only a few days allowed in between cities for transit and setup. No, we really could not afford any setbacks. And yes, a lot of “faith prayers” were uttered during every trip (or were they “presumptive proclamations”—not sure—maybe a mix of the two). An old split rim tire mounted on an old bus Once we got to Tampa, attempting to be frugal, I visited the junkyards hoping to find a used replacement rim. As if they had conspired to dissuade me, every junkyard owner/manager shot down my hopes with a similar assessment, “Fella, you won’t find one of them old split-rims anywhere. They’re dangerous. When you try to mount a tire on one, they can snap open and injure somebody real bad, cutting off a hand, even killing a person. We melted ‘em all down as scrap metal.” (Go ahead, look them up online—they were even called “widow-makers.”) It was the same story everywhere I went. Nobody could help. Then three weeks passed and we had to pack the bus and head to our next location—Bessemer City, North Carolina. It was a college-level, biblically-sound course on developing long-suffering and patience: stopping every thirty miles or so to air up that unpredictable tire, pleading with God to somehow supernaturally assist us in our journey by making sure none of the tires blew. Somehow, we made it—around 600 miles—stopping about 25 times. Then an incredible miracle happened! God did it and I still feel awestruck, just writing about it. As we turned into the fairgrounds area, right in the middle of the entrance were two brand new, neatly-stacked truck tires (unclaimed), exactly the size we used on the bus—mounted (you guessed it!) on the very same split rims our bus required. Talk about worshiping God—we launched into a praise session right then and there! What were the odds? We all knew it had to be God. 麦克史瑞夫 80年代的帐篷会议是我55年来的焦点,在美国和14个其他国家担任部长。 上帝在耶稣革命期间(1970年)从嬉皮的生活方式和热情中怜悯地拯救了我,尽管通过远东宗教实践(瑜伽和冥想)错误地追求真理.

在遇到耶稣和被送走后不久,我与上帝的另一个兄弟一起,开始搭便车到全国各地,在街角和大学校园传福音. 多年来,这在教堂、礼堂、会议和帐篷十字军中发展成部。

超自然的供给和神的干预 总是让我在五年半的历险历程中 然而,以下的故事是一个经典的故事. 大约25年来,我在全国各地搭载着大型福音帐篷。

在这个“奇迹”发生时,我正用一辆老旧、破旧的公交车将60×90的帐篷从一个城市运送到另一个城市,这辆公交车不断给我们的业余技工技能带来新的挑战(轻轻地推开)。 有一天,在前往佛罗里达州坦帕的路上——不幸地——我们撞上了路边的一个大坑洞,在后左侧竖起一个大型卡车轮胎,后侧有严重的凹痕。

从此,内管不会保留空气,使得每30英里左右必须停一次才能再次填充. . . 再加上问题, 另一台后轮胎是秃头, 因此,一个公寓会 使我们完全停顿。

有时,我想起那些时候(那时我们对王国的热情超越了我们可能拥有的任何智慧),我惊讶地看到,无论怎样,上帝总是照顾我们(就像他那慈爱的天父)。

数千磅的设备被装进那辆呻吟、颤抖、生锈、破烂的巴士——重型帆布帐篷路段、金属杆、木桩、平台和300张椅子——而且只有几天时间允许在城市之间过境和布置。 不,我们真的无法承受任何挫折。

在每次旅行中都发表了许多“信仰祷告”(或它们是否“假定的宣告”——不确定——可能是两者的混合)。 一辆旧公共汽车上挂着一个旧的分叉轮圈轮胎 一旦我们到了坦帕, 试图节俭, 我参观了垃圾场 希望找到一个旧的替代轮圈。

就像他们密谋劝阻我一样, 每个垃圾场老板/经理都用类似的评估来击落我的希望, “伙计, 他们很危险。 当你试图安装一个轮胎, 他们可以撕开和伤害一个人 真正的坏,切断一只手,甚至杀死一个人。

我们把它们都融化成废金属。” 他们甚至被称为“寡妇制造者”。 我去过的地方都一样 没人能帮上忙 然后三个星期过去了,我们不得不收拾公交车 并前往下一个地点——北卡罗莱纳州的贝瑟默市。

这是一个关于发展长期痛苦和耐心的大学级、圣经般的教程:每隔30英里左右就停下来吹吹那个不可预测的轮胎,恳求上帝以某种超自然的方式协助我们的旅程,确保没有轮胎爆炸。 不知何故,我们大约在600英里的距离里,停了25次。 奇迹发生了!

上帝做到了,我仍然感觉 西车,只是写它。 当我们变成广场时, 就在入口的中间, 两个全新的, 整洁的卡车轮胎(无人认领), 说到崇拜上帝——我们发起了一次赞美会议,

什么机会? 我们都知道那是真主。耶和华已满足了。 他令人惊奇地承诺“超越一切, 然后说

title: Rejoice in the Lamb: Benjamin Britten, Christopher Smart, and the Poetry of Faith
summary: When music meets poetry, the result can be more than art, it can become an expression of spiritual wonder. The last time I heard Professor Bruce Redford speak about the eccentric British clergyman and poet Christopher Smart (1722–1771), I was so inspired that I included a substantial portion of Smart’s extraordinary poem, Jubilate Agno, in […]  The post  Rejoice in the Lamb: Benjamin Britten, Christopher Smart, and the Poetry of Faith  first appeared on  God Reports .
summary_zh:
当音乐与诗歌相遇时,结果可以超越艺术,成为精神奇迹的体现.

上次我听到布鲁斯·雷德福德教授 谈到古怪的英国神职人员和诗人克里斯托弗·斯马特(1722–1771)时,我受到很大启发,在[.]中包含了一大部分斯马特非凡的诗歌,大庆阿格诺. 以及《信仰之诗》,
title_zh: 喜悦羔羊：本杰明·布里顿、克里斯托弗·斯马特和信仰的诗歌
content: When music meets poetry, the result can be more than art, it can become an expression of spiritual wonder. Christopher Smart The last time I heard Professor Bruce Redford speak about the eccentric British clergyman and poet Christopher Smart (1722–1771), I was so inspired that I included a substantial portion of Smart’s extraordinary poem, Jubilate Agno , in my book Beauty (And the Banana) . I described Smart as a theopoet , someone whose deep religious convictions found expression through a distinctive and imaginative poetic vision. Smart was no ordinary poet. His writings moved freely between the sacred and the seemingly mundane, finding divine significance in everything from biblical figures to animals and the natural world. His poetry was exuberant, unconventional, and, at times, wonderfully strange. For Smart, creation itself was a chorus of praise, and every living thing had a part to play. Recently, I had another opportunity to hear Redford explore Smart’s remarkable literary legacy, this time through the music of British composer Benjamin Britten (1913–1976). As part of an All Saints’ Day concert at the Cathedral of St. John in Albuquerque, New Mexico, celebrating Britten’s music, Redford delivered a pre-concert lecture focusing on the composer’s Rejoice in the Lamb , a choral masterpiece that brings Smart’s unusual poetry to life. The evening offered a fascinating intersection of literature, music, theology, and history, demonstrating how two artists separated by nearly two centuries could share a common vision of wonder. The Musical Imagination of Benjamin Britten Benjamin Britten. Photo: Public Domain. Redford, a former professor at Boston University who was living in England when Britten died in 1976, identified three defining characteristics of the composer’s work. First, Britten’s music is distinguished by “passion and variety.” His compositions resist easy categorization, moving between emotional intensity, dramatic storytelling, and moments of remarkable spiritual intimacy. Redford described Britten’s approach as creating a kind of musical parable, pointing to Curlew River , one of Britten’s church parables, as a particularly compelling example. Second, Britten demonstrated an extraordinary ability to balance “economy and scope.” Redford compared this quality to the novels of Jane Austen, whose carefully constructed narratives reveal entire worlds through seemingly modest details. Similarly, Britten could communicate profound emotional and spiritual truths through restrained musical means. Nothing was wasted; every note served a purpose. Third, and perhaps most important for the evening’s performance, Britten possessed an exceptional “sensitivity to words.” Redford described him as an “inspired” interpreter of literary texts, a composer who understood that music should not merely accompany poetry but illuminate its deeper meaning. It was this third characteristic that led Redford to Christopher Smart. When an Eccentric Poet Meets a Brilliant Composer In 1943, Britten composed Rejoice in the Lamb (Op. 30), a festival cantata scored for four soloists, SATB choir, and organ. The composition draws its text from Smart’s Jubilate Agno , a work of religious poetry that remained largely unknown for nearly two centuries. Christopher Smart Smart wrote much of the poem during his confinement in a private madhouse in eighteenth-century London. Its unconventional structure, biblical references, exuberant language, and seemingly spontaneous declarations of praise made it unlike almost anything else in English religious literature. The manuscript remained unpublished until W. F. Stead brought it to public attention in 1939. Soon afterward, the poet W. H. Auden introduced Britten to Smart’s newly published work while the composer was living in the United States. The connection proved fruitful. Britten recognized something remarkable in Smart’s poetry: an unrestrained celebration of creation that could be translated into music.
content_zh:
当音乐与诗歌相遇时,结果可以超越艺术,成为精神奇迹的体现. 克里斯托弗·聪明 上次我听到布鲁斯·雷德福德教授谈到古怪的英国神职人员和诗人克里斯托弗·斯马特(1722–1771)时,我深受启发,在我的书《美人(和香蕉)》中包含了一大部分斯马特非凡的诗集《阿格诺大庆》。

我形容Smart是一位戏剧家, 聪明不是普通诗人 他的著作在圣人和看似庸俗的人之间自由移动,在从圣经人物到动物和自然世界的一切事物中都发现了神圣的意义.

他的诗歌充满了活力,与众不同,有时也非常奇怪. 对于Smart来说,创作本身是赞美的合唱,每一个活物都有角色可以扮演. 最近,我又有机会听到雷德福德探索Smart杰出的文学遗产,这次是通过英国作曲家本杰明·布里顿的音乐(1913–1976).

作为新墨西哥州阿尔布开克圣约翰大教堂庆祝布列顿音乐的全圣人节音乐会的一部分,雷德福德发表了一场音乐会前演讲,重点讲述了作曲家在羊羔中的欢乐,这是一部将斯马特不寻常的诗歌带给人生的奇特杰作.

晚上提供了文学、音乐、神学和历史的奇妙交汇点,展示了两个艺术家如何在将近两个世纪的时间里分开,可以分享一个共同的奇观。 本杰明·布林顿·本杰明·布林顿的音乐想象. 图片:公共域名.

雷德福德(Redford)是波士顿大学前教授,1976年布里顿逝世时居住在英国,他确定了作曲家作品的三个决定性特征. 首先,布列顿的音乐以“热情和多样性”来区分。 他的构思抵制轻松的分类,在情感的强度,戏剧性的故事性,以及非凡的精神亲密的时刻之间移动.

Redford将布列顿的做法描述为创造了一种音乐比喻,指向了布列顿教堂比喻之一的Curlew River,作为特别有说服力的例子.

第二,Britten表现出了平衡“经济和范围”的非凡能力。 雷德福德将这种品质与简·奥斯汀的小说相比较,他精心构建的叙事通过看似微小的细节揭示了整个世界. 同样,布列顿可以通过受约束的音乐手段传达深刻的情感和精神真理. 没有浪费任何东西;每张纸条都有作用。

第三,或许对晚间演出来说最重要的,布列顿拥有一种非凡的“言语敏感性 ” 。 Redford将他描述为文学文本的“受启发的”解释者,他是一个作曲家,他明白音乐不应仅仅伴随着诗歌,而应阐明其更深层次的意义。 正是这第三个特征导致雷德福找到克里斯托弗·斯马特.

1943年,当一位爱心诗人遇到一位杰出的作曲家时,布列顿在"羔羊"(Op. 30)中编曲了"欢乐"(Rejoice in the Lamb (Op. 30)),一个节日的Cantata为四位独奏家,SATB合唱团和管风琴打分. 内容来自Smart's Jubilate Agno, 一部宗教诗歌作品,

克里斯托弗·斯马特(Christopher Smart Smart)在18世纪伦敦一个私人疯人院禁闭期间写下了这首诗的大部分内容. 它的非常规结构,圣经的参考文献,兴旺的语言,以及看似自发的赞美宣言,使得它几乎不同于英国宗教文献中的其他任何内容. 手稿直到W. F.

施泰德在1939年引起了公众的注意. 不久之后,诗人W·H·奥登(W. H. Auden)在作曲家在美国居住期间,向布里顿介绍了斯马特新出版的作品. 这种联系证明是富有成果的。 Britten在Smart的诗歌中承认了一些令人瞩目的事物:一种可以被翻译成音乐的无限制的创作庆典.

summary_zh: “我的教父是教宗！” 一年半前，罗伯特·普雷沃枢机主教当选为教宗时，那些曾以朋友、神父或主教的身份认识这位美国传教士的秘鲁人欣喜若狂。但对于米尔德来说，
title_zh: 我的教父是教宗！| 国家天主教登记册
content: ‘My Godfather Is the Pope!’ When Cardinal Robert Prevost was elected Pope a year and a half ago, Peruvians who had known the American missionary as a friend, pastor or bishop were elated. But for Mildred Camacho, the moment was even more surreal, given who the man now known as Leo XIV has always been to her: her godfather. “I still can’t believe, even now, that the same person I’ve admired since I was young … is the Holy Father,” said Camacho, who is now 31 years old, just a year older than Prevost was when he served as a missionary priest in her hometown of Chulucanas from 1985 to 1986. A Lasting Connection The origin of their connection began that same year, when Father Prevost led a group of altar boys in the small town in the far north of Peru. The head altar server was a boy named Hector Camacho, who developed a deep admiration for the American missionary and would go on to become Mildred’s father. Like other members of the group, Hector stayed in touch with Father Prevost after he left Chulucanas. The two reunited when the American returned to Peru to serve from 1988 to 1999 in Trujillo, about an eight-hour drive from Chulucanas. In 1995, when Hector’s wife was pregnant, he asked Father Prevost if he could name his daughter after Father Prevost’s late mother, Mildred. The priest said, “Yes.” Then, soon after Mildred was born, Hector asked the busy missionary if he would serve as her godfather. Hector recalled that Father Prevost accepted without hesitation — but was also keen to get it on the calendar. “Let’s set a date, because I don’t travel to Chulucanas often,” Hector recalls Father Prevost telling him. So the date was set: Aug. 17, 1996, a few days after Mildred’s first birthday. Father Prevost arrived around 8 p.m., accompanied by a small group of seminarians. After the ceremony, they all enjoyed a celebratory dinner, with Father Prevost and company staying until 1 a.m. “He came and was present, not as a priest celebrating Mass, but as a godfather,” Hector recalled. A Missionary Godfather Growing up, Mildred knew her godfather mostly through photos, as well as letters he would send that her dad would read to her. When Father Prevost became the prior general of the Augustinian order (2000-2012), he would send her emails from the countries he visited. She said their first in-person meeting took place when she was 6 years old, when Prevost visited a Catholic youth ministry and mission center in the Chulucanas area. They’ve seen each other a few other times throughout the years, with their last meeting being in 2024, when then-Cardinal Prevost returned to Chulucanas for a celebration of the diocese’s 60th anniversary. But even though she hasn’t spent much time with him in person, she feels her godfather has carried out his role in her life effectively. She pointed to the profound witness of missionary zeal and service to those most in need that has marked his ministry, which she has followed over the years. “As a spiritual guide, I feel that he has done his job very well, and not only for me,” she said. A Surreal Day On May 8, 2025, Mildred got a message from her godmother to tune in to coverage of the papal conclave: White smoke was coming from the Vatican. She pulled it up on her phone. “I felt very nervous; I was shaking, I was moving around,” she recalled. She knew that Cardinal Prevost had been mentioned in news coverage as a possible papal candidate. When they announced his name, nervousness gave way to elation. “I called my dad right away. ‘Dad, he won, he won!’ ‘What, what?’ ‘My godfather is the Pope!’ And he started shouting and I was crying.” She says it was the first time she has ever cried from joy. “I said, ‘Thank you, my God, thank you! You have the best ally here on earth to help with the work.’” Sharing Her Story Growing up, Mildred would show people photos of her godfather with popes like St. John Paul II or Benedict XVI. Others would acknowledge the connection, she said, but would quickly move on. But

和小组的其他成员一样,赫克托在离开楚卢卡纳斯后与普雷沃斯特神父保持联系. 两人在1988至1999年美国人返回秘鲁在特鲁希略服役时团聚了,大约从楚卢卡纳斯开车8小时. 1995年,赫克托的妻子怀孕后,他问普雷沃斯特神父是否可以以普雷沃斯特神父已故母亲米尔德雷德的名字取出他的女儿的名字.

牧师说:是的。 之后,在米尔德丽德出生后不久,赫克托就问了忙碌的传教士是否愿意担任她的教父. 赫克托回忆道,普雷沃斯特神父毫不犹豫地接受了——但也热衷于将其列入日历. 赫克托回顾普雷沃斯特神父告诉他, 于是定了日期:奥古.

17, 1996, 米尔德丽一岁生日后几天, 普雷沃斯特神父于晚上8时左右抵达,由一小群神学院士陪同. 仪式后,他们都享受了庆典晚宴,由普雷沃斯特神父和伴同住到凌晨一点. 赫克托回忆说,“他不是作为牧师庆祝弥撒,而是作为教父来到并在场”。

一个传教士教父长大成人,穆德丽多通过相片认识她的教父,以及他寄给她的由她爸爸给她看的信. 当普雷沃斯特神父成为奥古斯丁教令(2000-2012年)的先行将领时,他会从他访问过的国家发送她的电子邮件.

她说,他们第一次当面会面是在她6岁时进行的,当时普雷沃斯特拜访了楚卢卡纳斯地区的天主教青年部和传教中心. 他们的最后一次会面是在2024年, 当时的Cardinal Prevost回到Chulucanas庆祝教区成立60周年。

她觉得她的教父在生活中有效地履行了他的职责。 她指出,她多年来一直注视着他的部,她深切地目睹了传教士的热情和为那些最需要帮助的人提供的服务。 她说,“作为精神导师,我认为他的工作做得非常好,而且不只是为了我。”

2025年5月8日,米尔德丽接到了教母的留言,要调和到教皇会堂的报导:白烟从梵蒂冈来. 她在手机上拉起来的 “我感到非常紧张;我在发抖,在四处走动,”她回顾道。 她知道,红衣主教普雷沃斯特在新闻报道中被指为可能的教皇候选人.

当他们宣布他的名字时,紧张让位给喜悦. “我马上打电话给我爸爸。 爸爸,他赢了,他赢了! 曰:"何为? 曰:"我教父为教宗! 他开始叫喊,我哭了。” 她说这是她第一次为欢乐而哭泣 "我说:"谢谢你,我的上帝,谢谢你!

title_zh: 利奥十四世在秘鲁感谢人们在他返乡时给予的热烈欢迎，并与信众一同祈祷
content: Basado en hechos observados y verificados directamente por nuestros periodistas o por fuentes informadas. Lima, 11 nov (EFE).- El papa León XIV agradeció este miércoles por la "acogida tan calurosa", al dirigirse a las cientos de personas que se acercaron a saludarlo en la Nunciatura Apostólica en Lim... El papa León XIV agradeció este miércoles por la "acogida tan calurosa", al dirigirse a las cientos de personas que se acercaron a saludarlo en la Nunciatura Apostólica en Lima, y rezó con ellos, antes de descansar al término de su primer día de visita en el país. "No tengo palabras para agradecer esa acogida tan calurosa de haber vuelto a mi casa", agregó León XIV, al celebrar la alegría y la oración con la que todos los asistentes lo esperaron durante varias horas. Luego, el Santo Padre pidió oraciones por la paz en el mundo y señaló que también "algunos quieren dormir (en el vecindario) y quieren paz", lo cual desató las risas de los presentes, entre ellos religiosas y jóvenes voluntarios en la visita papal. "Puede seguir la fiesta, pero no toda la noche", manifestó el papa, y procedió a rezar el padre nuestro y dar la bendición a todas las personas que lo esperaban en esta zona de la ciudad. Durante la tarde, los voluntarios animaron a los presentes con canciones y bailes mientras esperaban que el Santo Padre culmine con la agenda prevista tras su arribo a Lima. En todo el recorrido que ha hecho el Papa este miércoles, tanto en automóvil cerrado como en el 'papamóvil', unos tres millones de personas, según las autoridades peruanas citadas por el Vaticano, han salido a las calles de Lima a saludar su paso, con banderines y globos blancos y amarillos, los colores del Vaticano. En su primer día en el país, al que adoptó como segunda patria, León XIV visitó a la presidenta Keiko Fujimori en el Palacio de Gobierno, en el centro histórico de la ciudad, y luego acudió a un encuentro con otras autoridades y representantes diplomáticos en el Gran Teatro Nacional. Fujimori pide al Papa sus oraciones para gobernar con sabiduría y vocación de servicio La presidenta de Perú, Keiko Fujimori, pidió este miércoles al papa León XIV sus oraciones para que quienes tienen la responsabilidad de dirigir su país, como ella, sepan hacerlo con "sabiduría, humildad y auténtica vocación de servicio", además de confiar en que "el sufrimiento de ayer no siga gobernando" hasta la actualidad. Durante un discurso ofrecido en el Gran Teatro Nacional, Fujimori pidió también al Santo Padre que puedan encontrarse en la fe, en la buena voluntad y en el deseo sincero de construir "un país más justo, más fraterno y más unido". "Como usted mismo nos ha enseñado, perdonar no significa olvidar", afirmó la mandataria y añadió que tampoco significa "justificar el daño ni renunciar a la verdad y a la justicia". La gobernante afirmó que "significa encontrar la fortaleza interior para que el sufrimiento de ayer no siga gobernando nuestras vidas de hoy", para reforzar su capacidad de escuchar "a quien piensa distinto", de tender la mano a "quien ayer considerábamos un adversario" y de comprender que, por encima de las diferencias, los une el amor por el Perú. Fujimori afirmó que el Papa "conoce mejor que nadie el alma de nuestro pueblo" y que para seguir adelante "el Perú necesita sanar" sus heridas del pasado. En tal sentido, la jefa de Estado explicó que la reconciliación nacional no es un simple acuerdo político ni la imposición de una perspectiva particular, "ésta sólo será posible si empezamos a entender y resolver el dolor y la necesidad del prójimo". Afirmó que en sus viajes por el país sigue encontrando poblaciones que siguen sufriendo los "impactos negativos de la violencia terrorista, del abandono permanente del Estado y de la desigualdad" en la nación. Por otro lado, Fujimori recordó al joven sacerdote agustino de 29 años que dejó su Chicago natal en 1985 y llegó "al calor de Chulucanas", en el norte de Perú, donde León XIV empezó su trabajo como misionero en

summary: Papa León XIV regresa a Perú y lo llama su patria ante Keiko Fujimori; recuerda sus años como misionero y su nacionalidad peruana Durante su visita apostólica, el pontífice recordó los años que vivió
summary_zh: 教宗利奥十四世重返秘鲁，在凯科·藤森面前称之为自己的祖国；他回顾了自己作为传教士的岁月以及秘鲁国籍。在牧灵访问期间，教宗回顾了他在这里度过的岁月。
title_zh: 教宗利奥十四世重返秘鲁，在凯科·藤森面前称之为祖国；他回顾了自己作为传教士的岁月以及秘鲁国籍。
content: Papa León XIV regresa a Perú y lo llama su patria ante Keiko Fujimori; recuerda sus años como misionero y su nacionalidad peruana Durante su visita apostólica, el pontífice recordó los años que vivió en territorio peruano, donde desarrolló parte de su labor religiosa y obtuvo la nacionalidad en 2015 El papa León XIV regresó a Perú y expresó que considera al país parte de su propia historia, al que incluso llamó su patria durante su primer encuentro con las autoridades, encabezado por la presidenta Keiko Fujimori, en el Gran Teatro Nacional de Lima. “Me alegra profundamente volver al Perú”, fueron las primeras palabras del pontífice durante su intervención de este miércoles 11 de noviembre, en la que recordó los años que vivió en territorio peruano como misionero y posteriormente como obispo de Chiclayo. La información fue difundida por la agencia EFE. Uno de los momentos más significativos de su discurso ocurrió cuando explicó el vínculo que mantiene con el país sudamericano y reconoció que su regreso tiene un significado especial, luego de haber obtenido la nacionalidad peruana en 2015. “Por eso puedo decirles, con profunda gratitud, que regreso también a mi patria”, expresó ante los asistentes, quienes respondieron con aplausos. ¿Por qué el papa León XIV considera a Perú su patria? El pontífice, nacido en Chicago, Estados Unidos, explicó que su relación con Perú comenzó mucho antes de que fuera designado responsable de la Diócesis de Chiclayo, donde desarrolló una parte importante de su trayectoria religiosa. Durante su mensaje, recordó las experiencias que compartió con las comunidades peruanas y cómo estas influyeron en su vida personal y pastoral. - Años como misionero: León XIV recordó que compartió la vida cotidiana de los habitantes, escuchó sus preocupaciones y aprendió de su fe durante su estancia en el país. - La convivencia con las familias: relató que muchas personas le abrieron las puertas de sus hogares, compartieron sus alimentos y lo hicieron sentir parte de sus comunidades. - El recuerdo de la gastronomía peruana: incluso mencionó con humor que durante aquellos años también disfrutó de algunos buenos platos de ceviche, una de las preparaciones tradicionales del país. - Su nacionalidad: en 2015 recibió la ciudadanía peruana, un reconocimiento que, según explicó, formalizó un vínculo que ya existía desde mucho antes. “Hoy comprendo cuánto de esta tierra permanece conmigo y cuánto de mi propia historia les pertenece también a ustedes”, expresó. El recibimiento al papa León XIV en Perú La llegada del pontífice estuvo acompañada de muestras de afecto por parte de los asistentes, quienes dejaron de lado el protocolo habitual para expresar su entusiasmo por su regreso. El recibimiento también estuvo marcado por la participación de la presidenta Keiko Fujimori, quien encabezó la recepción oficial después de que el papa aterrizara procedente de Argentina. - Una bienvenida entre aplausos: durante su llegada, algunas personas comenzaron a corear “El papa es de Perú”, en referencia a los años que vivió en ese territorio. - Un gesto durante la recepción: el pontífice acompañó a la mandataria durante la interpretación del himno nacional peruano. - Encuentro con las autoridades: posteriormente, ambos participaron en las actividades oficiales y se trasladaron al Gran Teatro Nacional, donde se desarrolló el encuentro con representantes del Gobierno, la sociedad civil y el cuerpo diplomático. León XIV recuerda su pasado antes de hablar como líder de la Iglesia católica Aunque ahora regresa con una responsabilidad diferente, como Sucesor de Pedro y máxima autoridad de la Iglesia católica, León XIV reconoció que sus experiencias en Perú forman parte de su historia y de su formación como pastor. El pontífice señaló que, si tuviera la oportunidad de recorrer nuevamente aquellos años, lo haría con alegría, aceptando tanto los momentos felices como las dificultades que encontró durante su labor religiosa. content:
2026 다니엘기도회 18일차 간증 강사: 최유라 전도사 약할 때 강함 되시는 주님 본문: 고린도후서 12장 9–10절 “내 은혜가 네게 족하도다 이는 내 능력이 약한 데서 온전하여짐이라”.

1. 태어나는 순간부터 시작된 고난, 왜 하필 나였을까

저는 세 자매 중 막내딸로 태어났습니다. 어머니는 저를 임신하셨을 때 원인을 알 수 없는 심한 복통에 시달리셨습니다. 교회에 다니지 않으셨지만 고통이 너무 심해 할머니를 따라 새벽예배에 나가셨고, 하나님께 간절히 기도하셨습니다.

“하나님, 이 아이를 하나님께 바치겠습니다.”

그러나 제가 태어난 순간, 분만실에는 축하 인사 대신 무거운 침묵이 흘렀습니다. 제 몸의 절반 이상이 붉은 반점으로 뒤덮여 있었기 때문입니다. 저는 ‘클리펠-트레노네-베버 증후군’이라는 선천성 희귀질환을 가지고 태어났습니다. 포도주색 반점과 혈관 기형, 신체 일부의 비대가 나타나는 질환이었습니다.

어머니는 하나님을 원망하셨습니다. 하나님께 바치겠다고 서원한 아이가 왜 이런 모습으로 태어났는지, 이해할 수 없으셨습니다. 절망이 너무 깊어 저를 안고 아파트 8층에서 뛰어내리려는 생각까지 하셨습니다.

그러나 그 순간 하나님께서 어머니 마음을 만져 주셨습니다. 이후 어머니는 저를 숨기거나 부끄러워하지 않으셨습니다. 오히려 어디를 가든 저를 데리고 다니셨고, ‘우리 집 점순이’라며 자랑하셨습니다.

초등학교에 들어가면서 저는 다른 아이들과 제 모습이 다르다는 사실을 뼈저리게 깨달았습니다. 친구들은 저를 괴물, 외계인, 귀신, 보라돌이, 좀비라고 불렀습니다. 그 말들이 제 마음을 찢어 놓았습니다.

사람들을 피하기 시작했습니다. 과자를 사러 슈퍼에 가고 싶어도 누군가 마주칠까 두려워, 복도에서 발걸음을 떼지 못했습니다. 엘리베이터에서 인기척이 들리면 급히 집 안으로 들어갔습니다. 집은 저를 놀리는 사람이 없는 유일한 안식처였습니다.

2. 사라지지 않는 붉은 반점, 죽고 싶었던 어린 시절

어린 시절 저의 가장 간절한 소원은 붉은 반점이 사라지는 것이었습니다.

누군가 된장을 바르면 반점이 없어진다고 했습니다. 부모님은 매일 밤 제 얼굴에 된장을 발라 주셨습니다. 냄새가 지독했지만 참았습니다. 반점만 없앨 수 있다면 무엇이든 할 수 있었습니다.

하나님께도 간절히 기도했습니다. “하나님, 제 얼굴에 있는 붉은 반점을 없애 주세요.”

예수님이 병든 사람들을 고치셨다는 이야기를 들었기에, 저도 고쳐 주실 것이라 믿었습니다. 그러나 얼굴을 씻을 때마다 거울 속 제 모습은 변함없었습니다.

어느 날 기독교 서점에 갔을 때였습니다. 그곳에 있던 어른이 제 얼굴을 보고 왜 그러느냐고 물었습니다. 저도 이유를 모른다고 대답하자, 어머니가 임신했을 때 포도주를 많이 마셔서 그렇다고 말씀하셨습니다.

저는 서점 밖으로 나와 엉엉 울었습니다. 제 모습이 어머니의 잘못 때문이라는 말을 받아들일 수 없었습니다. 달리는 자동차 앞으로 뛰어들고 싶을 만큼 절망스러웠습니다.

학창 시절에도 상처는 계속됐습니다. 롯데월드에 갔을 때 친구들은 신나게 놀았지만, 저는 사람들을 피해 오락실에 숨어 집에 돌아갈 시간만 기다렸습니다. 다른 사람들에게는 환상의 나라였지만, 제게는 두려움의 장소였습니다. 저는 제 자신이 너무 싫었습니다. 팔에 상처를 내기도 했고, 몇 차례 극단적 선택을 시도하기도 했습니다.

학교에 가는 것은 그저 하루를 견디는 일이었습니다. 공부할 의욕도 없고 성적은 늘 하위권이었습니다. 공부를 못하는 것이 아니라, 공부해야 할 이유를 찾지 못했던 것입니다.

“하나님, 왜 저를 이렇게 만드셨습니까? 도대체 저보고 어떻게 살아가라는 것입니까?”

3. 고등학교 2학년 겨울, 살아야 할 이유를 발견하다

제 인생의 전환점은 고등학교 2학년 겨울 수련회에서 찾아왔습니다.

저는 어릴 때부터 교회에 다녔습니다. 선생님들은 하나님이 저를 사랑하신다고 말씀하셨지만, 그 말씀이 마음에 와닿지 않았습니다. 하나님이 정말 저를 사랑하신다면 왜 이런 모습으로 태어나게 하셨는지 이해할 수 없었습니다.

그런데 수련회에서 예수 그리스도의 십자가가 제 마음에 다가왔습니다. 예수님이 저의 죄를 대신해 십자가에 못 박히셨다는 사실이 머리로만 이해되는 것이 아니라 마음으로 믿어지기 시작했습니다.

“하나님은 나를 한 번도 포기하지 않으셨구나. 하나님은 내 모습 그대로를 사랑하시는구나. 나는 하나님의 귀한 자녀구나.”

저는 스스로를 보잘것없고 끔찍한 존재라고 생각했습니다. 그러나 하나님은 저를 보석처럼 귀하게 여기시는 분이셨습니다.

그 순간 살아야 할 이유가 생겼습니다. 시편 118편 17절 말씀이 제 마음에 새겨졌습니다. “내가 죽지 않고 살아서 여호와께서 하시는 일을 선포하리로다.”

이제는 죽고 싶은 사람이 아니라, 살아서 하나님의 영광을 선포하는 사람이 되고 싶었습니다.

삶의 목적이 생기자 행동도 달라졌습니다. 학교에 가면 먼저 말씀을 묵상하고 지혜를 달라고 기도했습니다. 버스 안에서 영어 단어를 외웠고, 식사하면서 인터넷 강의를 들었습니다.

성적이 오르기 시작했습니다. 하위권에서 중위권으로, 다시 상위권으로 올라갔습니다. 이후 신학대학교에 입학했고, 성적 장학금을 계속 받으며 조기 졸업했습니다. 신학대학원에서도 총장상을 받으며 졸업했습니다.

그런데 어느 순간 문제가 생겼습니다.

처음에는 하나님의 사명을 위해 공부했지만, 점점 사람들에게 인정받는 것이 좋아졌습니다. 성적이 좋으면 가치 있는 사람이 된 것 같았고, 성적이 떨어지면 제 존재까지 초라해지는 것 같았습니다. 예전에는 외모 때문에 자신을 미워했다면, 이제는 성적과 성취로 제 가치를 증명하려 했습니다.

4. 죽음의 문턱에서 깨달은 하나님의 은혜

무리한 생활이 계속되면서 몸에 이상이 나타났습니다.

원인을 알 수 없는 고열이 반복되었고, 검사 결과 심장을 둘러싼 심막에 물이 차 있다는 사실을 알게 되었습니다. 곧바로 입원해 물을 빼내는 시술을 받았습니다.

그러나 시술 후에도 물이 제대로 빠지지 않았습니다. 여러 병원을 거쳐 결국 삼성서울병원에서 수술과 조직검사를 받았습니다. 혈관 구조가 일반적인 경우와 달라 여러 진료과의 협진이 필요했습니다.

수술 후에도 고통은 끝나지 않았습니다.

일주일 뒤 심장 초음파 검사를 받던 중 갑자기 극심한 가슴 통증이 찾아왔습니다. 식은땀이 쏟아지고 혈압이 떨어졌습니다. 검사 결과 혈관이 터져 흉강에 피가 고여 있었습니다.

응급실에서 의료진이 긴급 처치를 시작했습니다. 혈관을 찾기 어려워 여러 부위에 주삿바늘을 꽂아야 했습니다. 흉강에 고인 피를 빼내기 위해 관을 삽입하는 과정은 말로 표현하기 어려울 만큼 고통스러웠습니다.

그때 처음으로 강하게 느꼈습니다.

‘살고 싶다.’

그동안 죽고 싶다는 생각을 수없이 했지만, 실제로 죽음이 가까워지자 살아야겠다는 마음이 간절해졌습니다.

중환자실에서는 혼자 몸을 움직이는 것조차 어려웠습니다. 산소 공급 장치와 여러 의료기기에 의지해야 했습니다. 제가 할 수 있는 일은 하나님을 바라보며 기도하는 것뿐이었습니다.

그런데 일주일 뒤 다시 수술해야 한다는 말을 들었습니다. 몸속에 고인 피가 굳어 제거해야 한다는 것이었습니다.

그 순간 제 마음이 완전히 무너졌습니다.

“하나님, 도대체 저에게 왜 이러십니까? 이제 그만 저를 내버려 두시면 안 됩니까?”

의사에게 수술하지 않겠다고 소리쳤습니다. 이제까지 충분히 아팠고 견뎠다고 생각했습니다. 더 이상 버틸 힘이 남아 있지 않았습니다.

그러나 두려움 속에서 저는 다시 하나님을 붙잡았습니다. 병원 예배실에서 찬양하고 기도하던 시간은 제 인생에서 가장 간절하게 하나님을 찾았던 순간이었습니다.

그때 깨닫기 시작했습니다.

지금까지 저는 노력과 의지와 열심으로 제 존재를 증명하려 했습니다. 무엇인가를 이뤄야만 가치 있는 사람이 된다고 생각했습니다. 그러나 병원 침대에 누워 아무것도 할 수 없게 되었을 때에도 저는 하나님의 사랑받는 자녀였습니다.

5. 약할 때 강함이 된다는 말씀의 참된 의미

저는 고린도후서 12장 10절 말씀을 오랫동안 이해하지 못했습니다.

“이는 내가 약한 그 때에 강함이라.”

제 삶에서 약함은 언제나 약함으로 끝나는 것 같았습니다.

2026年但以理祷告会第18天见证分享讲员：崔有罗传道在软弱时成为力量的主经文：哥林多后书12章9-10节“他说：‘我的恩典够你用的。因为我的能力是在人的软弱上显得完全。’” 1. 从出生的那一刻就开始的苦难，为什么偏偏是我？

我是三个姐妹中最小的女儿。母亲怀我的时候，饱受原因不明的剧烈腹痛折磨。她不去教会，但因为疼痛太厉害，她就跟着奶奶去参加晨祷，并向神恳切祷告。“神啊，我愿意将这个孩子献给您。”

然而，在我出生的那一刻，分娩室里弥漫的不是欢庆的喜悦，而是沉重的沉默。因为我身体的一半以上都布满了红色斑点。

我天生患有一种名为“Klippel-Trenaunay-Weber综合征”的罕见疾病。这是一种会出现葡萄酒色斑、血管畸形和身体局部肥大的疾病。母亲怨恨神。她不明白，她发愿要献给神的孩子为什么会以这样的样子出生。绝望之情过于深重，她甚至想抱着我从公寓的8楼跳下去。然而，就在那一刻，上帝感动了母亲的心。此后，母亲不再把我藏起来，也不再感到羞耻。相反，她走到哪里都带着我，还骄傲地称我为“我们家的点顺（小美人）”。上小学后，我深刻地意识到自己与别的孩子不一样。朋友们叫我怪物、外星人、鬼、紫娃娃、僵尸。

那些话撕裂了我的心。我开始躲避人们。即使我想去超市买零食，也害怕会碰到别人，所以不敢走出走廊。如果听到电梯里有人走动的声音，我就会匆忙地回到家里。家是我唯一一个没有人嘲笑我的避风港。2. 不会消失的红色斑点，想死的童年

我童年时期最迫切的愿望就是让红斑消失。有人说，涂上大酱，红斑就会消失。父母每天晚上都会在我脸上涂抹味噌。虽然味道很重，但我忍住了。只要能消除红斑，我什么都愿意做。我也恳切地向神祷告。

“神啊，请您祛除我脸上的红斑。”

我听说耶稣治好了病人的病，所以我相信祂也会治好我。然而，每次洗脸时，镜子里的我都没有变化。有一天，我去了一家基督教书店。店里的一位成年人看到我的脸，问我为什么会这样。我回答说我也不知道原因，他说是因为我妈妈怀孕时喝了很多葡萄酒。我走出书店，放声大哭。我无法接受我的长相是母亲的错这种说法。我感到绝望至极，甚至想冲到疾驰的汽车前面。在学生时代，我仍然不断受到伤害。

去乐天世界的时候，朋友们玩得很开心，但我却躲在游戏厅里避开人群，只等着回家的时间。对其他人来说，那里是梦幻乐园，但对我来说，那里是充满恐惧的地方。我非常讨厌自己。我曾在手臂上划伤自己，还曾几次试图做出极端的选择。上学对我来说只是熬过一天而已。我没有学习的动力，成绩也总是很差。这不是因为我学不进去，而是因为我找不到学习的理由。“神啊，您为什么把我造成这样？您到底是要我怎么活下去？”

3. 高中二年级的冬天，找到了活下去的理由

我人生的转折点出现在高二的冬季培灵会。我从小就去教会。

我的老师告诉我上帝爱我，但这些话并没有引起我的共鸣。我不明白，如果上帝真的爱我，为什么他会让我这样出生。但在静修中，耶稣基督的十字架来到了我的心中。我开始不仅用头脑理解，而且用心相信耶稣为我的罪被钉在十字架上。 “上帝从未放弃过我。上帝爱我本来的样子。我是上帝宝贵的孩子。”

我认为自己是微不足道的、可怕的。然而，上帝看重我就像珍宝一样。那一刻，我有了活下去的理由。诗篇 118:17 铭刻在我的心上。

“我不会死；我会活着并宣扬主所做的事。”

现在，我不想成为一个想死的人，而是想成为一个活着并宣扬上帝荣耀的人。一旦我有了人生目标，我的行为就会改变。当我上学时，我首先默想神的话语并祈求智慧。我在公交车上背英语单词，边吃饭边听网络讲座。我的成绩开始提高。它从底部到中间，然后又到顶部。后来，我进入神学院并提前毕业，同时继续获得优秀奖学金。他还以总统奖毕业于神学研究生院。但在某个时候，问题出现了。起初我是为了神的使命而学习，但渐渐地我开始喜欢被人认可。

如果我的成绩好，我会觉得自己成为了一个有价值的人，但如果我的成绩差，我会觉得我的存在变得很寒酸。过去，我因为自己的外表而讨厌自己，但现在我试图通过成绩和成就来证明自己的价值。 4. 神的恩典在临死之际实现

随着不合理的生活方式的持续，我的身体开始出现异常。不明原因的高烧再次出现，检查显示心脏周围的心包充满了水。我立即住院并接受了排水手术。然而，即使在手术之后，水也没有正常排出。去了几家医院后，我最终在三星首尔医院接受了手术和活检。由于血管结构与典型病例不同，需要多科室协作。手术后疼痛并未结束。

一周后，在接受超声心动图检查时，我突然感到胸口剧烈疼痛。我出了一身冷汗，血压也下降了。检查结果显示，血管破裂，胸腔内积血。急诊室里，医护人员开始紧急救治。由于很难找到血管，因此必须将针插入多个区域。插管引流胸腔积血的过程，痛苦到难以用言语表达。那是我第一次强烈地感受到这种感觉。 “我想活下去。”

我曾多次想过要死，但随着死亡的临近，我求生的欲望也越来越强烈。在重症监护室里，我一个人连移动身体都困难。我不得不依靠氧气供应和一些医疗设备。我所能做的就是仰望上帝并祈祷。

但一周后，我被告知需要再次接受手术。体内积聚的血液已经凝固，需要排除。那一刻我的心彻底崩溃了。 “上帝啊，你为什么要这样对我？你现在就不能放过我吗？”

我对医生大喊我不做手术。我以为到目前为止我已经忍受了足够多的痛苦。我已经没有力气再坚持下去了。但在我的恐惧中，我再次抓住了上帝。我在医院小教堂里赞美祷告的那段时间，是我一生中最恳切寻求神的时刻。就在那时我开始意识到。到目前为止，我一直试图用努力、意志和热情来证明我的存在。我认为我必须取得一些成就才能成为一个有价值的人。

但即使我躺在医院的病床上，无法做任何事，我仍然是神所爱的孩子。 5.“当我们软弱时，我们就会变得坚强”这句话的真正含义。

我很长一段时间都不明白哥林多后书 12:10。 “当我软弱时，我就会坚强。”

在我的一生中，软弱似乎总是以软弱告终。耶稣

title_zh: K-CCM 选拔赛“治愈之声”将于 20 日进行决赛直播
content:
TOP7 우승자 가릴 최종 라운드 마지막 무대 미션은 ‘나의 고백’ 힐링멘토 점수와 유튜브 점수, 퐁당 실시간 투표 합산해 결정 ‘혼자 걷지 않을 거예요’ 합동 무대

선교 미디어 CGN은 K-CCM 글로벌 오디션 '힐링보이스'의 파이널 라운드 생방송을 오는 11월 20일(금) 오후 8시부터 진행한다.

이번 파이널에서 TOP7 보이스 김성결, 김호준, 나시온, 아삽, 이철규, 장근희, 호림 등은 마지막 미션 ‘나의 고백’ 무대를 선보인다.

최종 우승자는 생방송 무대 힐링멘토 점수, 방송 중 진행되는 퐁당 실시간 투표 점수(1인 1회만 가능)에, 지난 5라운드 경연에 대한 힐링멘토 점수와 관객 점수, 방송 직후 공개한 신곡 무대의 유튜브 점수(좋아요, 조회수) 합산으로 결정된다.

지난 세미파이널 현장 순위는 7위 아삽(총점 644점: 힐링멘토 점수 455점, 관객 점수 189점), 6위 호림(총점 680점: 힐링멘토 점수 463점, 관객 점수 217점), 5위 이철규(총점 681점: 힐링멘토 점수 455점, 관객 점수 226점), 4위 나시온(총점 724점: 힐링멘토 점수 470점, 관객 점수 254점), 3위 김성결(총점 748점: 힐링멘토 점수 459점, 관객 점수 289점), 2위 김호준(총점 750점: 힐링멘토 점수 462점, 관객 점수 288점), 1위 장근희(총점 794점: 힐링멘토 점수 495점, 관객 점수 299점) 등이었다.

파이널 무대에 따라 결과가 얼마든지 뒤집힐 수 있는 만큼, 생방송에 대한 시청자들의 관심은 더욱 높아지고 있다.

각 보이스의 ‘나의 고백’ 미션은 마지막 무대인만큼, 각자의 신앙고백을 담은 혼신의 찬양을 올릴 예정이다.

이날 방송은 축제와 파송의 현장으로 꾸며진다. 힐링멘토와 보이스들의 특별무대가 다수 준비된다. 방송 마지막에는 전체 출연 보이스들이 함께 엔딩곡 ‘혼자 걷지 않을 거예요’를 부르며, 모두가 순위를 넘어 같은 길을 걷는 믿음의 동역자임을 확인하는 시간을 가진다.

또 무대 위 출연자들이 객석을 위로하고 객석과 힐링멘토들이 보이스들의 앞날을 축복하는 시간이 될 예정이다.

파이널 생방송은 CGN TV, 기독 OTT ‘퐁당(fondant)’과 유튜브에서 동시 방송되며, 온라인 화상 프로그램 줌(ZOOM)으로 국내외 20개 지역에 동시 연결된다. 생방송 중 실시간 투표는 퐁당에서만 참여할 수 있으며, 1인 1회만 가능하다.

파이널 무대의 음원은 12월 13일부터 각종 음원사이트(멜론, 지니, 스포티파이, 유튜브 뮤직)에서 들을 수 있다.
content_zh:
决赛的最终阶段任务将通过《我的告白》治愈导师评分、YouTube评分和翻糖实时投票相结合的方式决出TOP7获胜者。 《我不会独行》联合舞台

Mission Media CGN 将于 11 月 20 日星期五晚上 8 点直播 K-CCM 全球选秀《Healing Voice》决赛。在本次决赛中，TOP7配音金成杰、金浩俊、纳西翁、亚萨、李哲奎、张根熙、浩林将执行最后的任务“我的告白”。最终获奖者由现场治愈导师评分、播出期间举行的翻糖实时投票评分（每人限一次）、过去5轮比赛的治愈导师评分和观众评分以及播出后立即发布的新歌舞台的YouTube评分（点赞和观看次数）之和确定。

最后半决赛现场排名为第七名亚萨（总分644分：治愈导师评分455分、观众评分189分）、第六名霍林（总分680分：治愈导师评分463分、观众评分217分）、第五名李哲奎（总分681分：治愈导师评分455分、观众评分226分）、第4名 Nasion（总分：724分：治愈导师评分：470分、观众评分：254分）、第3名：金成杰（总分：748分：治愈导师评分：459分、观众评分：289分）、第2名金浩俊（总分：750分：治愈导师评分：462分、观众评分：288）分）、第一名张根熙（总分：794分：治愈导师分数为495分，观众分数为299分）等。由于最终结果可能会被推翻，观众对直播的兴趣正在增加。

由于每个声音的“我的告白”任务是最后阶段，每个声音都会用他们的全身来歌颂他们的信仰告白。这一天的广播充满了节日和新闻的场景。还将准备许多由治愈导师和声音带来的特别表演。节目结束时，所有主播齐声合唱片尾曲《我不会独行》，每个人都花时间确认自己是超越阶级的信仰伙伴，走在同一条路上。这也将是舞台上的表演者安慰观众和观众、治愈导师祝福声音未来的时刻。决赛直播将在中广核电视台、Christian OTT《翻糖》、YouTube同步播出，并通过在线视频节目ZOOM同步连线国内外20个地区。

直播期间的实时投票只能在翻糖上进行，并且每人只能进行一次。从12月13日开始，最终舞台的音源可以在各种音乐网站（Melon、Genie、Spotify、YouTube Music）上听到。

summary_zh: 11月11日，奥克兰平安教会举行成立仪式暨侨民联合聚会李泰熙总会长：“祷告是福音的根基”李基道牧师：“团结起来，开展宣教合作”11月11日（当地时间），民族福音化运动本部新西兰本部在新西兰奥克兰平安教会举行了成立仪式暨奥克兰侨民联合聚会，正式开启教会联合、下一代信仰传承、韩民族侨民福音化工作。本次活动以“在基督耶稣里合而为一（AS ONENESS IN CHRIST JESUS）”为主题，韩国代表团、新西兰当地牧师、总部负责人以及侨民信徒共同出席。与会者通过崇拜和祷告，分享了新西兰福音化、朝鲜半岛和平、福音统一、世界宣教等使命。值此2027年——1907年平壤大复兴120周年暨1977年民族福音化大圣会50周年之际，新西兰本部回顾了这些信仰遗产，并开展了悔改、祷告和传福音的活动。
title_zh: 民族福音化运动新西兰总部成立……“在福音中合而为一，走向万邦”
content:
11월 11일 오클랜드 평강교회 발대식 및 교민 연합집회 개최 이태희 총재 “기도, 복음의 뿌리” 이기도 목사 “연합해 선교 협력”

사단법인 민족복음화운동본부 뉴질랜드본부가 지난 11월 11일(현지시간) 뉴질랜드 오클랜드 평강교회에서 발대식 및 오클랜드 교민연합집회를 열고, 교회 연합과 다음 세대 신앙 계승, 한민족 디아스포라 복음화에 본격 나섰다.

‘그리스도 예수 안에서 하나됨(AS ONENESS IN CHRIST JESUS)’을 주제로 마련된 이번 행사에는 한국 방문단과 뉴질랜드 현지 목회자, 본부 임원, 교민 성도들이 함께했다. 참석자들은 예배와 기도를 통해 뉴질랜드 복음화와 한반도 평화, 복음통일, 세계 선교 등의 사명을 나눴다.

뉴질랜드본부는 1907년 평양대부흥 120주년이자 1977년 민족복음화대성회 50주년인 2027년을 맞아, 이러한 신앙의 유산을 돌아보며 회개와 기도, 복음 전도의 사명을 새롭게 하고, 2027년 8천만 민족복음화대성회를 위한 해외 협력에 적극 동참하기로 했다.

발대식에서 민족복음화운동본부 총재 이태희 목사는 “멀리 떨어져 있어도, 복음 안에서 우리는 하나”라고 문안했다. 그는 부득이한 사정으로 현장에 함께하지 못한 아쉬움을 전하며, 자신을 대신해 참석한 강복렬 부총재와 이기도 상임준비위원장, 김호승 홍보기획총괄준비위원장 등을 통해 감사와 축복의 마음을 전한다고 밝혔다.

이태희 목사는 언어와 문화의 차이 속에서도 예배의 자리를 지키고 자녀들의 손을 잡고 교회로 향했던 교민 성도들의 수고를 격려했다. 특히 “여러분이 지켜온 작은 기도의 자리가 오늘 뉴질랜드 땅에 복음의 뿌리를 내리는 소중한 밑거름이 됐다”고 격려했다.

이 목사는 영상 격려사에서 “뉴질랜드 한인교회와 성도들은 그 땅의 이웃을 사랑하고 섬기는 동시에, 조국과 북한 동포를 위해 기도하는 선교의 동역자”라며 “뉴질랜드본부가 교회들을 기도로 연결하고, 다음세대가 부모 세대의 믿음을 자신의 신앙으로 고백하도록 돕는 통로가 되기를 바란다”고 전했다.

또 “북한 동포들의 아픔을 기억하면서, 한반도 평화와 복음통일을 위해 함께 기도해 달라”며 “오늘의 예배가 다음 날 전도로 이어지고, 발대식에서 맞잡은 손이 지속적인 동역으로 이어지기를 바란다”고 당부했다.

2027년 8천만 민족복음화대성회 상임준비위원장이자 어명세계선교회 대표인 이기도 목사는 축사에서 이번 뉴질랜드본부 출범은 하나님께서 맡기신 복음 전파의 사명을 다시 확인하고, 세계선교를 향한 새로운 출발을 다짐하는 자리”라고 정의했다.

이기도 목사는 “8천만 민족복음화 비전이 대한민국 국민과 북한 동포, 세계 각지 한민족 디아스포라를 품는 데서 출발해, 모든 민족에게 복음을 전하는 사명으로 이어질 것”이라며 “마가복음 16장 15절 말씀처럼, 복음 전파는 모든 교회가 함께 감당해야 할 사명”이라고 강조했다.

그는 “뉴질랜드본부가 한인교회와 현지 교회, 목회자와 선교사들을 연결하며 뉴질랜드 복음화와 세계선교에 협력하는 전초기지가 되길 바란다”며 “교회와 교단의 경계를 넘어 연합하고, 세대와 지역을 넘어 협력하며, 한 영혼이라도 더 주님께 인도하는 데 힘써야 한다”고 권면했다.

이 목사는 “주님의 재림을 기다리는 믿음이 선교의 실천으로 이어져야 한다”며 “뉴질랜드에서 시작된 복음의 사역이 오세아니아를 넘어 세계로 확장돼, 이사야 6장 8절의 부르심에 응답하는 헌신이 일어나길 기도한다”고 전했다.

뉴질랜드본부 대표본부장 데보라 정 목사는 취임사에서 한민족이 복음으로 하나 되고, 성령의 능력으로 복음을 전하며, 다음 세대에 신앙을 온전히 계승하는 일을 사명으로 제시했다.

데보라 정 목사는 “권위보다 섬김을, 경쟁보다 연합을, 사람의 이름보다 예수 그리스도의 이름을 높이겠다”며 “한국과 뉴질랜드 양국 교회가 서로 기도하고 협력하며, 교단과 교파를 넘어 한 영혼이라도 더 주님께 인도하는 선교 공동체로 함께 서자”고 촉구했다.

이날 행사는 1부 예배, 2부 발대식 및 축하의 시간, 저녁식사 후 3부 오클랜드 교민연합집회로 구성됐다.

1부 예배는 평강교회 이복만 목사 사회로 오클랜드한인교회협의회 회장 정재식 목사의 대표기도, 선성훈 장로의 성경봉독, 어명선교워십팀의 감사워십에 이어 민족복음화운동본부 부총재 강복렬 목사가 ‘여호와의 권능이 내게 임하여(에스겔 40:1-4)’를 제목으로 말씀을 전했다.

데이빗 고 목사는 헌금기도 후 신다니엘 목사가 인도한 특별기도에서는 △대한민국과 북한, 전 세계 디아스포라의 구원 △2027년 대성회와 한국교회의 회복 및 부흥 △세계 선교와 열방 선교사들을 위한 기도 등을 놓고 기도했다. 1부 예배는 예수사랑선교센터 대표 김영수 목사의 축도로 마쳤다.

2부 발대식은 윤정규 목사 사회로 민족복음화운동본부 소개 영상과 처치 언리미티드(Church Unlimited) 탁 바나(Tak Bhana) 목사의 영상 축사, 임명장 수여, 취임사와 축하 순서가 마련됐다. 강복렬 목사가 대표본부장 데보라 정 목사를 비롯한 임원들에게 임명장을 수여했다.

민족복음화운동본부 홍보기획총괄본부장 김호승 목사는 “해외에서 가정을 이루고 교회를 지키며 다음세대에 복음을 전해 온 교민 성도들의 헌신에 존경과 감사를 전한다”며 “뉴질랜드본부가 교회와 교회를 잇고 세대와 세대의 손을 잡아주는 연합의 통로가 되기를 소망한다”고 축사했다.

김호승 목사는 “서로의 형편을 돌아보고 지친 사역자를 격려하며, 복음을 알지 못하는 이웃에게 먼저 다가가는 공동체가 교민 사회일수록 절실할 것”이라며 “현장의 기도와 헌신을 성실하게 전해, 더 많은 교회와 성도가 민족복음화 사역에 동참하도록 힘쓰겠다”고 밝혔다.

2027년 대성회 상임대회장 김대성 목사는 서면 축사에서 데보라 정 목사와 ‘기도행전’에서 함께 기도하며 교제해 온 인연을 소개했다. 기도의 자리에서 맺어진 만남이 바다를 넘어 복음을 위한 동역으로 이어진 데 감사를 전하며, 뉴질랜드본부가 현지 교회를 기도로 연결하고 다음세대와 한민족 디아스포라를 품는 통로가 되기를 당부했다.

현지 교계 지도자들도 축사를 통해 뉴질랜드본부 출범을 축하하고 지속적 선교 협력을 요청했다. 오클랜드한인교회협의회 회장 정재식 목사는 “한인들뿐 아니라 뉴질랜드에서 함께 살아가는 다양한 민족과 이웃들에게 복음의 문이 열리기를 소망한다”며 “교회들이 서로 사역을 인정하고 격려하며, 다음 세대를 세우고 지역사회를 섬기는 실제 사역으로 협력하자”고 전했다.

다니엘선교센터 이사장 이은태 목사는 “복음은 민족과 나라를 변화시키는 하나님의 능력”이라며 “뉴질랜드 한인 교회들과 현지 교회들이 세대와 교파의 차이를 넘어 연합해, 2027년 대성회가 화해와 회복, 다음세대 신앙 계승의 계기가 되기를 소망한다”고 말했다.

평강교회 안정기 목사는 회개와 기도를 통한 영적 회복을 강조하며 뉴질랜드와 대한민국에 새로운 부흥이 일어나기를 기원했다. 지구촌선교센터 선우형식 목사는 한국교회 부흥과 기도운동을 돌아보며, 뉴질랜드 한인들이 복음통일과 세계 복음화를 위해 합심기도를 이어가자고 권면했다.

탁 바나 목사는 영문 축사를 통해 뉴질랜드본부 출범을 축하하고, 뉴질랜드에 예수 그리스도의 복음을 전하려는 비전에 감사를 표했다. 한국 방문 당시 함께 복음을 전했던 기쁨을 돌아보며, 민족복음화운동의 영혼 구원 사역 위에 하나님의 은혜와 능력이 더해지기를 기원했다.

저녁식사 후 오클랜드 교민연합집회는 이복만 목사 사회로 고창범 목사의 기도, 강복렬 목사의 축사, 에스더 조 선교사의 성경봉독, 어명선교워십팀의 워십 순서 후 이기도 목사가 ‘천상의 비전을 보는 자가 세상을 이긴다(요한계시록 5:1-10)’는 제목으로 말씀을 전하고 축도했으며, 설교 후 윤근재 목사가 헌금기도를 맡았다.

이번 성회는 민족복음화운동본부 한국본부와 오클랜드한인교회협의회, 어명세계선교회, 갈릴리소명교회, 소생교회, 주예수이름교회, 뉴질랜드 평강교회, 뉴질랜드 비전침례교회, 뉴질랜드 선한이웃교회, 다니엘선교센터, 지구촌선교센터, 북한인권개선위원회, 쥬빌리통일구국기도회 등의 협력기관 및 단체들이 함께했다.

뉴질랜드본부는 대표본부장 데보라 정 목사를 중심으로 현지 교회와 동역자들의 기도와 협력을 이어가며, 뉴질랜드
